title.zh: 卷二十八 志第九: 禮一 郊
title.raw: 卷二十八 志第九: 禮一 郊 Volume 28 Treatises 9: Rites 1 - Jiao

sentences.zh: 金人之入汴也，時宋承平日久，典章禮樂粲然備具。

translations.literal: When the Jin entered Bian, the Song had long enjoyed peace; statutes, ritual, and music stood complete and bright.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin took Bian, the Song had known peace for generations—law, ritual, and music all in full array.

sentences.zh: 金人既悉收其圖籍，載其車輅、法物、儀仗而北，時方事軍旅，未遑講也。

translations.literal: The Jin had gathered all their maps and registers, loaded chariots, ritual objects, and regalia northward; they were still at war and had no leisure to study rites.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the archives and hauled chariots, regalia, and ceremonial gear north, but armies still marched—rites could wait.

sentences.zh: 既而，即會甯建宗社，庶事草創。

translations.literal: Soon after, at Huining they founded the state; every affair was freshly begun.
translations.idiomatic: At Huining they raised the altars of state; everything was built from scratch.

sentences.zh: 皇統間，熙宗巡幸析津，始乘金輅，導儀衛，陳鼓吹，其觀聽赫然一新，而宗社朝會之禮亦次第舉行矣。

translations.literal: In the Huangtong era, Emperor Xizong toured Xijin, first rode the golden chariot, led guards and insignia, arrayed drums and pipes—the spectacle wholly renewed, and the rites of state and court were performed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huangtong, Xizong visited Xijin, first took the golden chariot, drew up escort and insignia, set drums and pipes—the sight wholly new, and court and state ritual followed step by step.

sentences.zh: 繼以海陵狼顧，志欲併吞江南，乃命官修汴故宮，繕宗廟社稷，悉載宋故禮器以還。

translations.literal: Then came Hailing, wolf-glancing, intent to swallow the south; he ordered officials to repair the old Bian palace, mend ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain, and load back all the Song ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing came next, restless and hungry for Jiangnan; he rebuilt the Bian palaces, restored temple and altars, and shipped every Song ritual vessel home.

sentences.zh: 外行黷武，內而縱欲，其猷既失，奚敢議禮樂哉！

translations.literal: Outwardly reckless in arms, inwardly indulgent in desire—policy already lost, who dared speak of ritual and music!
translations.idiomatic: War without and appetite within—policy was gone; who could still debate ritual and music?

sentences.zh: 世宗既興，複收向所遷宋故禮器以旋，乃命官參校唐、宋故典沿革，開「詳定所」以議禮，設「詳校所」以審樂，統以宰相通學術者，於一事之宜適、一物之節文，既上聞而始匯次，至明昌初書成，凡四百餘卷，名曰《金纂修雜錄》。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong rose, he again recovered the Song ritual vessels moved away, ordered officials to collate Tang and Song precedents and their changes, opened a "Detailed Determination Office" to debate rites and a "Detailed Review Office" to examine music, all under learned chancellors; each matter's fitness and each object's protocol were reported upward before compilation—by early Mingchang the work stood complete, over four hundred juan, titled Jin Miscellaneous Records of Compilation and Revision.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong recovered the Song vessels that had been moved away and set scholars to collate Tang and Song ritual law. A Detailed Determination Office debated rites; a Detailed Review Office audited music—learned chancellors presiding. Nothing was entered until the throne had heard each fit and form. By early Mingchang the corpus stood: four hundred-odd juan, the Jin Miscellaneous Records of Compilation and Revision.

sentences.zh: 凡事物名數，支分派引，珠貫棋布，井然有序，炳然如丹。

translations.literal: All things' names and numbers, branched and linked, strung like pearls, laid like chess—orderly and clear, bright as cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: Names and numbers branched and threaded, pearl-strung and chess-set—orderly, luminous as vermilion.

sentences.zh: 又圖吉、凶二儀：鹵簿十三節以備大葬，小鹵簿九節以備郊廟。

translations.literal: They also charted auspicious and inauspicious regalia: thirteen sections of funeral escort for great burial, nine sections of lesser escort for suburban temple.
translations.idiomatic: They charted auspicious and inauspicious display: thirteen sections of funeral escort for state burial, nine of lesser escort for suburban and temple rites.

sentences.zh: 而命尚書左右司、春官、兵曹、太常寺各掌一本，其意至深遠也。

translations.literal: They ordered the Left and Right Offices of the Secretariat, Spring Office, Military Bureau, and Temple of Grand Harmony each to keep a copy—the intent ran very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the Secretariat's left and right offices, the Spring Office, Military Bureau, and Grand Harmony Temple kept a copy—the design ran deep.

sentences.zh: 是時，宇內阜安，民物小康，而維持幾百年者實此乎基。

translations.literal: Then within the realm was peace, the people modestly secure, and what sustained the dynasty for centuries was truly rooted here.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was calm, life modestly easy—and centuries of endurance rested on this foundation.

sentences.zh: 鳴呼，禮之為國也信矣夫！

translations.literal: Alas, that ritual as a state is trustworthy indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—ritual as the backbone of a state is no empty claim.

sentences.zh: 而況《關雎》、《麟趾》之化，其流風遺思被於後世者，為何如也。

translations.literal: How much more the transforming influence of "Guan Ju" and "Lin Zhi"—its lingering wind and far-reaching thought covering later ages—what may that be compared to.
translations.idiomatic: And what of the transforming air of "Guan Ju" and "Lin Zhi," its after-wind and long memory on later ages—what measure holds that?

sentences.zh: 宣宗南播，疆宇日蹙，旭日方升而爝火之燃，蔡流弗東而餘燼滅矣！

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong fled south, the realm shrank day by day; the sun rose while torch-flame still burned, the Cai current did not flow east and the last embers died!
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong fled south; the borders closed in. Dawn rose while torches still burned; the Cai stream never ran east again, and the last embers went out.

sentences.zh: 圖籍散逸既莫可尋，而其宰相韓企先等之所論列，禮官張暐與其子行簡所私著《自公紀》，亦亡其傳。

translations.literal: Registers scattered beyond recovery; what Chancellor Han Qixian and others had set forth, and Ritual Officer Zhang Wei with his son Xingjian's private Record from the Duke, also lost transmission.
translations.idiomatic: The archives were lost. Han Qixian's memorials, Ritual Officer Zhang Wei's work, and his son Xingjian's private Record from the Duke—all vanished from transmission.

sentences.zh: 故書之存，僅《集禮》若干卷，其藏史館者又殘缺弗完，姑掇其郊社宗廟諸神祀、朝覲會同等儀而為書，若夫凶禮則略焉。

translations.literal: What books remain are only several juan of Collected Rites; what the Historiography Office holds is again broken and incomplete—here we gather suburban, altar, ancestral temple, spirit worship, court audience, and assembly rites into a book; inauspicious rites are omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Only fragments of Collected Rites survive; the Historiography copy is broken. This treatise gathers suburban, altar, temple, spirit cult, audience, and assembly rites; inauspicious rites are passed over.

sentences.zh: 蓋自熙宗、海陵、衛紹王之繼弑，雖曰「鹵簿十三節以備大葬」，其行乎否耶？

translations.literal: From Xizong, Hailing, and the Prince of Wei and Shao's succession of regicide—though it is said "thirteen sections of funeral escort for great burial," were they performed or not?
translations.idiomatic: After Xizong, Hailing, and the murdered Prince of Wei and Shao—though the code speaks of "thirteen sections of funeral escort," who can say they were ever carried out?

sentences.zh: 蓋莫得而考也，故宣孝之喪禮存，亦不復紀。

translations.literal: None can be examined; thus Xuan Xiao's mourning rites survive in record but are not further chronicled.
translations.idiomatic: It cannot be verified; Xuan Xiao's funeral rites are noted but not fully recorded.

sentences.zh: 噫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 告朔餼羊雖孔子所不去，而史之缺文則亦慎之。

translations.literal: Though Confucius would not abandon the New Moon offering and the sacrificial sheep, the historian still is cautious where the text is missing.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius kept the New Moon sheep, yet the historian still treads lightly where the text breaks.

sentences.zh: 作《禮志》。

translations.literal: Thus the Treatise on Rites is composed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this Treatise on Rites.

sentences.zh: 南北郊

translations.literal: Southern and Northern Suburban Altars
translations.idiomatic: Southern and Northern Suburban Altars

sentences.zh: 金之郊祀，本於其俗有拜天之禮。

translations.literal: Jin suburban sacrifice grew from their custom of worshipping Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Jin suburban sacrifice grew out of the custom of worshipping Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其後，太宗即位，乃告祀天地，蓋設位而祭也。

translations.literal: Later, when Emperor Taizong took the throne, he announced sacrifice to Heaven and Earth—essentially setting seats and offering.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong succeeded, he announced Heaven and Earth—altars set, offerings made.

sentences.zh: 天德以後，始有南北郊之制，大定，明昌其禮浸備。

translations.literal: After Tiande, the southern and northern suburban system appeared; under Dading and Mingchang the rite gradually filled out.
translations.idiomatic: After Tiande came the southern and northern suburban system; under Dading and Mingchang the rite grew complete.

sentences.zh: 南郊壇，在豐宜門外，當闕之巳地。

translations.literal: The southern suburban altar stood outside Fengyi Gate, in the si position facing the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The southern suburban altar lay outside Fengyi Gate, in the si quarter opposite the palace.

sentences.zh: 圓壇三成，成十二陛，各按辰位。

translations.literal: The round altar had three tiers, twelve steps on each tier, each aligned to a chen position.
translations.idiomatic: The round mound rose three tiers, twelve steps per tier, each step set to its chen station.

sentences.zh: 濆牆三匝，四面各三門。

translations.literal: The moat-wall ran three circuits; on four sides three gates each.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred enclosure circled thrice; four faces, three gates each.

sentences.zh: 齋宮東北，廚庫在南。

translations.literal: The fasting palace lay northeast; storerooms and kitchens to the south.
translations.idiomatic: The fasting palace stood northeast; kitchens and stores to the south.

sentences.zh: 壇、濆皆以赤土圬之。

translations.literal: Altar and enclosure were both plastered with red earth.
translations.idiomatic: Altar and enclosure were plastered with red earth.

sentences.zh: 北郊方丘，在通玄門外，當闕之亥地。

translations.literal: The northern suburban square mound lay outside Tongxuan Gate, in the hai position facing the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The northern suburban square mound lay outside Tongxuan Gate, in the hai quarter opposite the palace.

sentences.zh: 方壇三成，成為子午卯酉四正陛。

translations.literal: The square altar had three tiers; steps at the four cardinal zi, wu, mao, and you positions.
translations.idiomatic: The square altar had three tiers with steps at zi, wu, mao, and you—the four cardinals.

sentences.zh: 方濆三周，四面亦三門。

translations.literal: The square sacred enclosure ran three circuits; four sides also had three gates.
translations.idiomatic: The square enclosure circled thrice; four sides, three gates each.

sentences.zh: 朝日壇曰大明，在施仁門外之東南，當闕之卯地，門濆之制皆同方丘。

translations.literal: The dawn sun altar, called Great Brightness, lay southeast outside Shiren Gate, in the mao position facing the palace; gate and enclosure matched the square mound.
translations.idiomatic: The dawn-sun altar Great Brightness stood southeast outside Shiren Gate, in the mao quarter—gates and enclosure like the square mound.

sentences.zh: 夕月壇曰夜明，在彰義門外之西北，當闕之酉地，掘地汙之，為壇其中。

translations.literal: The dusk moon altar, called Night Brightness, lay northwest outside Zhangyi Gate, in the you position facing the palace; the ground was dug and flooded to form the altar within.
translations.idiomatic: The dusk-moon altar Night Brightness stood northwest outside Zhangyi Gate, in the you quarter; the ground was dug and flooded to hold the mound within.

sentences.zh: 常以冬至日合祀昊天上帝、皇地祗於圜丘，夏至日祭皇地祇于方丘，春分朝日于東郊，秋分夕月於西郊。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice they jointly sacrificed to August Heaven, Supreme Lord, and Imperial Earth Sovereign at the round mound; on the summer solstice they sacrificed to Imperial Earth Sovereign at the square mound; at the spring equinox they greeted the sun at the eastern suburban altar; at the autumn equinox they sent off the moon at the western suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice: joint offering to August Heaven and Imperial Earth Sovereign at the round mound. Summer solstice: Earth Sovereign at the square mound. Spring equinox: the sun at the eastern suburban altar. Autumn equinox: the moon at the western suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 大定十一年始郊，命宰臣議配享之禮。

translations.literal: In Dading 11 they first performed suburban sacrifice and ordered the chancellors to debate accompanying offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Dading 11 brought the first suburban sacrifice; the throne ordered the chancellors to debate who should accompany the offering.

sentences.zh: 左丞石琚奏曰：「按《禮記》：'萬物本乎天，人本乎祖，此所以祖配上帝也。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Shi Ju memorialized: "According to the Book of Rites: 'The ten thousand things root in Heaven; man roots in his ancestors—therefore the ancestor is paired with August Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Shi Ju said: "The Book of Rites holds: 'All things root in Heaven; man roots in his ancestors—so the ancestor is paired with August Heaven.'

sentences.zh: '蓋配之者，侑神作主也。

translations.literal: 'To pair is to set the spirit a host.'
translations.idiomatic: "To pair is to give the spirit a host."

sentences.zh: 自外至者無主不止，故推祖考配天，尊之也。

translations.literal: 'What comes from without has no host and cannot rest—therefore push the founding ancestor to pair with Heaven, honoring him.'
translations.idiomatic: "What comes from without cannot rest without a host—so the founding ancestor is pushed up to pair with Heaven, in honor."

sentences.zh: 兩漢、魏、晉以來，皆配以一祖。

translations.literal: From the Two Han through Wei and Jin, all paired a single ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: From Han through Wei and Jin, a single ancestor was paired.

sentences.zh: 至唐高宗，始以高祖、太宗崇配。

translations.literal: Under Tang Gaozong, Gaozu and Taizong were first ennobled as paired spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Gaozong first paired Gaozu and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，又加以高宗，遂有三祖同配之禮。

translations.literal: In early Chuigong, Gaozong was added, and three ancestors shared one pairing.
translations.idiomatic: Early Chuigong added Gaozong—three ancestors on one altar.

sentences.zh: 至宋，亦嘗以三帝配，後禮院上議，以為對越天地，神無二主，由是止以太祖配。

translations.literal: Under Song they also once paired three emperors; later the Ritual Office memorialized that facing Heaven and Earth, the spirits accept no second lord—thereafter only Taizu was paired.
translations.idiomatic: Song too once paired three emperors; the Ritual Office later held that Heaven and Earth brook no second lord—only Taizu remained.

sentences.zh: 臣謂冬至親郊宜從古禮。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the winter solstice personal suburban sacrifice should follow the ancient rite."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds the winter solstice suburban sacrifice should follow antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「唐、宋以私親，不合古，不足為法。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Tang and Song favored private kinship—unlike antiquity, not fit to be law."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Tang and Song favored private kinship—not ancient law, not our model."

sentences.zh: 今止當以太祖配。

translations.literal: Now only Taizu should be paired."
translations.idiomatic: "Only Taizu shall be paired."

sentences.zh: 」又謂宰臣曰：「本國拜天之禮甚重。

translations.literal: He again told the chancellors: "Our state's worship of Heaven is weighty."
translations.idiomatic: He told the chancellors again: "Our worship of Heaven is weighty."

sentences.zh: 今汝等言依古制築壇，亦宜。

translations.literal: Now you speak of building altars by ancient rule—that too is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: "You urge altars by ancient rule—that too is fitting."

sentences.zh: 我國家絀遼、宋主、據天下之正，郊祀之禮豈可不行？

translations.literal: Our house ended Liao and Song, holds the Mandate's center—how can suburban sacrifice not be performed?"
translations.idiomatic: "Our house ended Liao and Song and holds the center of the realm—how can suburban sacrifice go unperformed?"

sentences.zh: 」乃以八月詔曰：「國莫大於祀，祀莫大於天，振古所行，舊章鹹在。

translations.literal: Then in the eighth month an edict said: "Nothing is greater than sacrifice for the state; nothing in sacrifice is greater than Heaven—carried from antiquity, the old statutes stand."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict ran: "For a state nothing outweighs sacrifice; in sacrifice nothing outweighs Heaven—antiquity's statutes still stand."

sentences.zh: 仰惟太祖之基命，詔我本朝之燕謀，奄有萬邦，於今五紀。

translations.literal: Looking up to the Founding Ancestor's mandate, he declared our dynasty's design; we hold the ten thousand regions, now five reign-periods.
translations.idiomatic: "We look up to the Founding Ancestor's mandate and our dynasty's design; the ten thousand regions are ours, five reigns on."

sentences.zh: 因時製作，雖增飾于國容，推本奉承，猶未遑於郊見。

translations.literal: Rites were fashioned to the times and though state display grew richer, pushing to the root and receiving Heaven, we still had not yet performed suburban audience.
translations.idiomatic: "Fashion followed the times and state display grew, yet receiving Heaven at the suburban altar still waited."

sentences.zh: 況天休滋至而年谷屢豐，敢不敷繹曠文、明昭大報。

translations.literal: Moreover Heaven's favor grows and harvests repeat—dare we not spread the vast text and proclaim the great return?"
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven's favor deepens, grain returns again—dare we not proclaim the great return?"

sentences.zh: 取陽升之至日，將親享於圓壇，嘉與臣工，共圖熙事。

translations.literal: Taking the day of yang's utmost ascent, I will personally offer at the round mound; rejoice with the ministers in this radiant affair."
translations.idiomatic: "On the day yang rises to its height I shall offer at the round mound; ministers, share this radiant work."

sentences.zh: 以今年十一月十七日有事於南郊，咨爾有司，各揚乃職，相予肆祀，罔或不欽。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the eleventh month of this year there will be rites at the southern suburban altar—each office, lift your charge; aid my great sacrifice; let none be lax."
translations.idiomatic: "Eleventh month, day seventeen—rites at the southern suburban altar. Each office, lift your charge; aid the sacrifice; let none be lax."

sentences.zh: 」乃於前一日，遍見祖宗，告以郊祀之事。

translations.literal: On the day before, he visited all ancestors everywhere and announced the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, he visited every ancestral shrine and announced the suburban rite.

sentences.zh: 其日，備法駕鹵簿，躬詣郊壇行禮。

translations.literal: On the day, the full imperial escort was prepared; he went in person to the suburban altar to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: That day the full escort was arrayed; the emperor went in person to the suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 齋戒：用唐制。

translations.literal: Fasting and purification: Tang rules were used.
translations.idiomatic: Fasting followed Tang usage.

sentences.zh: 大祀，散齋四日，臻齋三日。

translations.literal: For a great sacrifice, dispersed fasting four days, perfected fasting three days.
translations.idiomatic: Great sacrifice: four days dispersed fasting, three days perfected fasting.

sentences.zh: 中祀，散齋二日，致齋一日。

translations.literal: For a middle sacrifice, dispersed fasting two days, perfected fasting one day.
translations.idiomatic: Middle sacrifice: two days dispersed, one day perfected.

sentences.zh: 天子親祀，皆前期七日，攝太慰誓亞終獻官、親王、陪祀皇族于宮省。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven personally sacrificed, seven days beforehand the Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies swore in the secondary and final offering officials, princes, and accompanying imperial kin in the palace quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven sacrificed in person, seven days ahead the Acting Grand Master swore in secondary and final offerers, princes, and accompanying kin in the palace.

sentences.zh: 皇族十五以上，官雖不至七品者亦助祭受誓。

translations.literal: Imperial kin fifteen and above, though rank did not reach seventh grade, also aided sacrifice and received the oath.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kin fifteen and older, even below seventh rank, aided sacrifice and took the oath.

sentences.zh: 又誓百官於尚書省。

translations.literal: The hundred officials were again sworn in at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials were sworn in again at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 攝太尉南向。

translations.literal: The Acting Grand Master faced south.
translations.idiomatic: The Acting Grand Master faced south.

sentences.zh: 司徒北向，監祭御史在西，監禮博士居東，皆相向。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education faced north; the supervising censor was west, the supervising ritual academician east—all facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education faced north; the supervising censor west, the supervising ritual academician east—each opposite the other.

sentences.zh: 太常卿、光祿卿在司徒後，重行北向。

translations.literal: The Director of Grand Harmony and the Director of Imperial Victuals stood behind the Minister of Education, double-ranked facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Directors of Grand Harmony and Imperial Victuals stood behind the Minister of Education, ranked north.

sentences.zh: 司天監、光祿丞、太廟令丞、大樂令丞、太官令丞、良醖令、廩犧令、郊社丞、司尊、太祝、奉禮郎、協律郎、諸執事官皆重行西上北向。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy, Imperial Victuals aides, Grand Temple aides, Grand Music aides, Imperial Kitchen aides, Chief Brewer, Granary and Victuals officer, suburban altar aide, ritual vessel keeper, grand invoker, ritual attendant, pitch officer, and all executive officials were double-ranked west-upper facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomy, victual aides, temple aides, music aides, kitchen aides, brewer, granary officer, suburban altar aide, vessel keeper, grand invoker, attendants, pitch officers, and all executives ranked west-upper, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 禮直官以誓文授攝太尉，乃誓曰：「維某年歲次某甲，某月，某日，某甲，皇帝有事于南郊，各揚其職。

translations.literal: The ritual attendant gave the oath text to the Acting Grand Master, who swore: "In such-and-such year, such cyclical sign, such month, such day, such cyclical day, the Emperor has business at the southern suburban altar—each perform your charge."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual attendant handed the oath to the Acting Grand Master, who swore: "Year such, cyclical day such, month such, day such—the Emperor has business at the southern suburban altar; each perform your charge."

sentences.zh: 其或不恭，國有常刑。

translations.literal: Whoever is not reverent—the state has fixed punishment."
translations.idiomatic: "Whoever is not reverent—the state has fixed punishment."

sentences.zh: 」禮直官贊曰：「七品以下官皆退。

translations.literal: The ritual attendant intoned: "Officials seventh grade and below all withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: The attendant intoned: "Officials seventh grade and below withdraw."

sentences.zh: 」餘皆再拜，退。

translations.literal: The rest all bowed twice and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rest bowed twice and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 誓于宮省之儀皆同。

translations.literal: The oath in the palace quarters followed the same pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The palace oath followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 於是，皇帝散齋于別殿。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor performed dispersed fasting in a separate hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then dispersed-fasted in a side hall.

sentences.zh: 前致齋一日，尚舍設禦坐于大安殿，當中南向。

translations.literal: One day before perfected fasting, the Palace Service set the imperial seat in the Great Peace Hall, centered facing south.
translations.idiomatic: One day before perfected fasting, the Palace Service set the imperial seat in Great Peace Hall, south-facing.

sentences.zh: 設東西房於禦坐之側，設禦幄于室內，施簾於楹下。

translations.literal: East and west chambers were set beside the seat; an imperial canopy inside, curtains hung below the pillars.
translations.idiomatic: East and west chambers flanked the seat; an inner canopy, curtains at the pillars.

sentences.zh: 享前三日，陳設小次。

translations.literal: Three days before the offering, the lesser resting pavilion was arranged.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before the offering, the lesser pavilion was staged.

sentences.zh: 享前一日，設拜褥，及皇帝版位、皇帝飲福位，及黃道氈褥，自玉輅下至升輿所。

translations.literal: One day before the offering, kneeling mats were set, with the Emperor's position, the Emperor's blessing-drink position, and yellow felt mats from the jade chariot down to the mounting place.
translations.idiomatic: The day before: kneeling mats, the Emperor's station, the blessing-drink station, yellow felt from the jade chariot to the mounting place.

sentences.zh: 及致齋之日，通事舍人引文武五品以上官，陪位如式。

translations.literal: On the day of perfected fasting, the Communications Officer led civil and military officials fifth grade and above to attend by formula.
translations.idiomatic: On perfected-fasting day, the Communications Officer led civil and military officials fifth grade and above to attend by formula.

sentences.zh: 諸侍衛之官，各服其器服，並結佩，俱詣閣奉迎。

translations.literal: Each guard officer wore his appointed gear, knotted insignia, and all went to the gate to receive the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Guard officers wore their gear, knotted insignia, and went to the gate to receive the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 上水二刻，侍中版奏「外辦」。

translations.literal: At the second water-mark, the Attendant-in-Chief reported "outer preparations complete."
translations.idiomatic: At the second water-mark the Attendant-in-Chief reported: "Outer preparations complete."

sentences.zh: 皇帝服袞冕，結佩，乘輿出，警蹕、侍衛如常儀。

translations.literal: The Emperor donned dark ceremonial robes, knotted insignia, rode out in the carriage with escort and guards as usual.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor donned dark robes, knotted insignia, rode out with escort as usual.

sentences.zh: 皇帝即御座，東向坐。

translations.literal: The Emperor took the seat, sitting east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: He took the seat, facing east.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人承傳，殿上下俱拜，訖，西面，贊「各祗候」。

translations.literal: The Communications Officer transmitted the order; above and below the hall all bowed; finished, turned west and intoned "each keep reverent waiting."
translations.idiomatic: The Communications Officer transmitted; court above and below bowed; then westward: "Each keep reverent waiting."

sentences.zh: 一刻頃，侍中跪奏：「臣某言，請降就齋。

translations.literal: After one quarter-mark, the Attendant-in-Chief knelt and reported: "Your servant so-and-so reports—please descend to fasting."
translations.idiomatic: After a quarter-mark the Attendant-in-Chief knelt: "Your servant reports—please descend to fasting."

sentences.zh: 」俛伏，興，還侍位。

translations.literal: He bowed low, rose, returned to attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed low, rose, returned to post.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降座，入室，群官皆退。

translations.literal: The Emperor left the seat, entered the chamber; all officials withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor left the seat and entered the chamber; officials withdrew.

sentences.zh: 諸執事官皆宿於正寢，治事如故，不弔喪問疾，不判署刑殺文字，不決罰罪人，不與穢惡事。

translations.literal: Executive officials lodged in the main quarters, handling affairs as usual but without mourning visits, without signing capital punishment documents, without judging criminals, without foul or unclean matters.
translations.idiomatic: Executives lodged in the main quarters and handled routine business—but no mourning calls, no capital sentences signed, no punishments judged, no foul work.

sentences.zh: 致齋日，惟祀事則行，餘悉禁。

translations.literal: On perfected-fasting day only sacrificial business proceeded; all else was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Perfected-fasting day: only sacrifice; all else forbidden.

sentences.zh: 已齋而闕者，通攝行事。

translations.literal: If an official was absent after fasting, another was deputized to act.
translations.idiomatic: An absent official after fasting was replaced by a deputy.

sentences.zh: 陳設：前祀五日，儀鸞、尚舍陳設齋宮。

translations.literal: Arrangements: five days before sacrifice, the Ceremonial Guard and Palace Service arranged the fasting palace.
translations.idiomatic: Staging: five days before sacrifice, Ceremonial Guard and Palace Service arranged the fasting palace.

sentences.zh: 有司設扈從侍衛次於宮東西。

translations.literal: The relevant office set escort and guard pavilions east and west of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Escort and guard pavilions were set east and west of the palace.

sentences.zh: 又設陪祀親王次宮東稍南，西向北上，宗室子孫位於其後。

translations.literal: They also set the accompanying princes' pavilion slightly south of the palace east, west-facing north-upper; imperial clansmen ranked behind.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying princes' pavilion lay slightly south of the palace east, west-facing north-upper; clansmen behind.

sentences.zh: 又設司徒亞終獻行事執事官次於壇南外濆門之西，東向北上，重行異位。

translations.literal: They also set the Minister of Education, secondary and final offerers, and executive officials' pavilion west of the outer sacred gate on the altar south, east-facing north-upper, double-ranked at separate stations.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education, secondary and final offerers, and executives had a pavilion west of the outer sacred gate, east-facing north-upper, double-ranked at separate stations.

sentences.zh: 又設天名房，在壇南外濆門之東，西向。

translations.literal: They also set the Heavenly Name chamber east of the outer sacred gate on the altar south, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Name chamber stood east of the outer sacred gate, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 大禮使次於其後，皆西向。

translations.literal: The Grand Ritual Commissioner ranked behind it, all west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ritual Commissioner behind it—all west-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設席大屋於壇外西北，駐車輅以備風雪。

translations.literal: They also set a great canopy northwest outside the altar to shelter the chariot against wind and snow.
translations.idiomatic: A great canopy northwest outside the altar sheltered the chariot from wind and snow.

sentences.zh: 祀前三日，尚舍設大次於東濆外門內道北，南向。

translations.literal: Three days before sacrifice, the Palace Service set the great pavilion north inside the eastern sacred gate, south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before sacrifice, the great pavilion stood north inside the eastern sacred gate, south-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設小次於壇下卯陛之北，南向。

translations.literal: They also set the lesser pavilion north of the mao steps below the altar, south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The lesser pavilion stood north of the mao steps below the altar, south-facing.

sentences.zh: 有司設饌幔於東濆中門之北，南向。

translations.literal: The relevant office set the offering canopy north inside the middle eastern sacred gate, south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The offering canopy was set north inside the middle eastern sacred gate, south-facing.

sentences.zh: 設兵衛，各服其器服，守衛濆門，每門二人。

translations.literal: They set military guards; each wore his gear and guarded the sacred gates, two per gate.
translations.idiomatic: Military guards wore their gear and held the sacred gates—two per gate.

sentences.zh: 郊社令帥其屬，埽除壇之上下及濆之內外。

translations.literal: The suburban altar director led his subordinates to sweep above and below the altar and inside and outside the sacred enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban altar director swept the altar and enclosure, above and below, inside and out.

sentences.zh: 乃為燎位，在南中濆東門之東，壇之巳位。

translations.literal: Then they made the fire-pit position east of the southern middle sacred gate's east side, at the altar's si position.
translations.idiomatic: They made the fire-pit east of the southern middle gate's east side, at the altar's si station.

sentences.zh: 又為瘞坎，在中濆內戌位。

translations.literal: They also made a burying pit inside the middle sacred enclosure at the xu position.
translations.idiomatic: They also dug a burying pit inside the middle enclosure at the xu station.

sentences.zh: 祀前二日，太樂令帥其屬，設登歌之樂於壇上稍南，北向。

translations.literal: Two days before sacrifice, the Director of Grand Music led his subordinates to set the ascent music on the altar slightly south, north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before sacrifice, Grand Music set the ascent choir slightly south on the altar, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 玉磬在午陛之西，金鐘在午陛之東，柷一在鐘前稍北，敔一在磬前稍北，東西相向，歌工次之，余工各位於縣後。

translations.literal: Jade chime west of the wu steps, bronze bell east of the wu steps; one sounding-block slightly north before the bell, one sounding-block slightly north before the chime, east and west facing; singers ranked after; other musicians each at their post behind the bells.
translations.idiomatic: Jade chime west of the wu steps, bronze bell east; sounding-blocks north of each; singers behind; other musicians at their stations behind the bells.

sentences.zh: 琴瑟在前，匏竹在後，於壇下第一等上，皆重行異位，北向。

translations.literal: Zithers before, gourd-pipes and bamboo after, on the altar's first tier below, all double-ranked at separate stations, north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Zithers forward, gourd and bamboo behind, on the first tier below—all double-ranked, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設宮縣樂南濆外門之外，八佾二舞表于樂前。

translations.literal: They also set palace music outside the southern sacred gate, eight rows of dancers before the music.
translations.idiomatic: Palace music stood outside the southern sacred gate; eight rows of dancers before the orchestra.

sentences.zh: 又設《采茨》樂於應天門前。

translations.literal: They also set the "Cai Ci" music before the Gate of Accepting Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: They also set the "Cai Ci" music before the Gate of Accepting Heaven.

sentences.zh: 祀前一日，奉禮郎升設皇帝版位於壇上辰巳之間，北向。

translations.literal: One day before sacrifice, the ritual attendant ascended and set the Emperor's position between chen and si on the altar, north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, attendants set the Emperor's station between chen and si on the altar, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設皇帝飲福位於其左稍卻，北向。

translations.literal: They also set the Emperor's blessing-drink position slightly withdrawn to its left, north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The blessing-drink station stood slightly left and withdrawn, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 又帥禮直官設亞終獻位於卯陛之東北，西向北上。

translations.literal: They also led ritual attendants to set the secondary and final offering stations northeast of the mao steps, west-facing north-upper.
translations.idiomatic: Secondary and final offering stations lay northeast of the mao steps, west-facing north-upper.

sentences.zh: 司徒位於卯陛之東，道南西向。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education's station lay east of the mao steps, south of the path, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education stood east of the mao steps, south of the path, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書、太常卿、光祿卿、禮部侍郎位各次之，太常丞、光祿丞又次之。

translations.literal: The Ministers of Rites, Grand Harmony, and Imperial Victuals ranked after in order; Grand Harmony and Imperial Victuals aides after them again.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of Rites, Grand Harmony, and Imperial Victuals followed; their aides after.

sentences.zh: 又設大禮使位於小次之左少卻，西向。

translations.literal: They also set the Grand Ritual Commissioner's station slightly withdrawn left of the lesser pavilion, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ritual Commissioner stood slightly left and withdrawn of the lesser pavilion, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設分獻官、司天監、讀冊中書侍郎位於中濆門道北，西向。

translations.literal: They also set the divided offering officials, Directorate of Astronomy, and Reader of the Memorial Vice Director of the Secretariat north of the middle sacred gate path, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Divided offering officials, Astronomy, and the Reader of the Memorial Vice Director stood north of the middle gate path, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 郊社令、廩犧令、太官令、良醖令位於其後。

translations.literal: The suburban altar director, granary and victuals director, imperial kitchen director, and chief brewer ranked behind.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban altar director, granary officer, kitchen director, and chief brewer ranked behind.

sentences.zh: 又設郊社丞、太祝、奉禮郎以下諸執事官位於其後，皆西向，重行異位。

translations.literal: They also set the suburban altar aide, grand invoker, ritual attendant, and all executive officials behind, all west-facing, double-ranked at separate stations.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban altar aide, grand invoker, attendants, and executives behind—all west-facing, double-ranked.

sentences.zh: 又設從祀文武群官一品至五品位於中濆門內道南，西向，皆重行立。

translations.literal: They also set accompanying civil and military officials first through fifth grade inside the middle sacred gate on the path south, west-facing, all double-ranked standing.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying officials first through fifth grade stood inside the middle gate, path south, west-facing, double-ranked.

sentences.zh: 又設助奠祝史齋郎位於東濆門外道北，西向。

translations.literal: They also set assisting offering invokers, recorders, and fast officers north outside the eastern sacred gate, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Assisting invokers, recorders, and fast officers stood north outside the eastern gate, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設陪祀皇族于道南，西向。

translations.literal: They also set accompanying imperial kin on the path south, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying imperial kin stood on the path south, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 六品至九品從祀群官，又于其南，皆西向，重行異位，各依其品。

translations.literal: Sixth through ninth grade accompanying officials ranked still farther south, all west-facing, double-ranked at separate stations by grade.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth through ninth grade officials stood farther south—west-facing, double-ranked by grade.

sentences.zh: 又設監祭御史二員，一員在午陛之西南，一員在子陛之西北，皆東向。

translations.literal: They also set two supervising censors—one southwest of the wu steps, one northwest of the zi steps, both east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Two supervising censors: one southwest of wu steps, one northwest of zi steps—both east-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設監禮博士二員，一員在午陛之東南，一員在子陛之東北，皆西向。

translations.literal: They also set two supervising ritual academicians—one southeast of the wu steps, one northeast of the zi steps, both west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Two supervising ritual academicians: southeast of wu, northeast of zi—both west-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設太樂令位於樂虡之間稍東，西向。

translations.literal: They also set the Director of Grand Music slightly east between the music frames, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Grand Music stood slightly east between the frames, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 協律郎位於樂虡之西，東向。

translations.literal: The pitch officer stood west of the music frame, east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch officer stood west of the frame, east-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設奉禮郎位於壇南稍東，西向。

translations.literal: They also set the ritual attendant slightly southeast on the altar south, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual attendant stood slightly southeast on the altar south, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 贊者次之。

translations.literal: Intoners ranked after.
translations.idiomatic: Intoners followed.

sentences.zh: 司尊位於酌尊所，俱北向。

translations.literal: The vessel keeper stood at the libation station, all north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The vessel keeper stood at the libation station—all north-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設牲榜於外濆東門之外，西向。

translations.literal: They also set the victim placard outside the outer eastern sacred gate, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The victim placard stood outside the outer eastern gate, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 饌榜於其北稍西，南向。

translations.literal: The offering placard slightly north and west of it, south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The offering placard lay slightly north and west, south-facing.

sentences.zh: 牲榜之東，牲位。

translations.literal: East of the victim placard, the victim position.
translations.idiomatic: East of the victim placard stood the victim station.

sentences.zh: 太史、太祝各位於牲後，俱西向。

translations.literal: The Grand Astrologer and grand invoker each at their post behind the victim, both west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer and grand invoker stood behind the victim, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設禮部尚書、太常卿、光祿卿位於牲榜南稍北，西向。

translations.literal: They also set the Ministers of Rites, Grand Harmony, and Imperial Victuals slightly north of the victim placard south, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of Rites, Grand Harmony, and Imperial Victuals stood slightly north of the victim placard, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 太常丞、光祿丞、太官令位於其後。

translations.literal: Grand Harmony aide, Imperial Victuals aide, and imperial kitchen director ranked behind.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Harmony aide, Imperial Victuals aide, and kitchen director behind.

sentences.zh: 監祭御史、監禮博士于禮部尚書位之西稍卻，北向。

translations.literal: Supervising censor and supervising ritual academician slightly withdrawn west of the Minister of Rites' position, north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor and ritual academician stood slightly west and withdrawn of the Minister of Rites, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 廩犧令位在牲位西南，北向。

translations.literal: The granary and victuals director stood southwest of the victim position, north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The granary officer stood southwest of the victim, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 又陳禮饌於榜之前案上。

translations.literal: They also displayed ritual offerings on the table before the placard.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual offerings were displayed on the table before the placard.

sentences.zh: 未後三刻，陳饌之時，又設禮部尚書、太常卿、光祿卿位於案前稍東，北上，西向。

translations.literal: At the third quarter-mark after wei when offerings were set, they also set the Ministers of Rites, Grand Harmony, and Imperial Victuals slightly east before the table, north-upper, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: At the third quarter after wei, when offerings were set, the three ministers stood slightly east before the table, north-upper, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 太常丞、光祿丞、太官令位於其後，西向。

translations.literal: Grand Harmony aide, Imperial Victuals aide, and imperial kitchen director ranked behind, west-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Their aides and the kitchen director behind, west-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設監祭御史、監禮博士位於案前稍西，北上，東向。

translations.literal: They also set supervising censor and supervising ritual academician slightly west before the table, north-upper, east-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor and ritual academician stood slightly west before the table, north-upper, east-facing.

sentences.zh: 又設異寶嘉瑞位於宮縣西北，太府少監位於寶後。

translations.literal: They also set exotic treasures and auspicious omens northwest of the palace music; the Vice Director of the Imperial Store stood behind the treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Exotic treasures and auspicious omens stood northwest of palace music; the Imperial Store vice director behind.

sentences.zh: 諸州歲貢位於宮縣東北，戶部郎中位於其後。

translations.literal: Each circuit's annual tribute stood northeast of the palace music; the Bureau of Revenue director ranked behind.
translations.idiomatic: Annual tribute from the circuits stood northeast of palace music; the Revenue Bureau director behind.

sentences.zh: 天子八寶位於宮縣西南，符寶郎八員各於寶後。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's eight treasures stood southwest of the palace music; eight seal officers each behind a treasure.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's eight treasures stood southwest of palace music; eight seal officers behind them.

sentences.zh: 伐國毀寶位於宮縣東南，少府少監位於其後。

translations.literal: Treasures taken from conquered states stood southeast of the palace music; the Vice Director of the Palace Workshops stood behind.
translations.idiomatic: Spoiled regalia of conquered states stood southeast; the Palace Workshops vice director behind.

sentences.zh: 又設大樂令位於宮縣之北稍東，協律郎二在大樂令南，東西相向。

translations.literal: They also set the Director of Grand Music slightly north and east of the palace music; two pitch officers south of the director, east and west facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Music stood slightly north and east of palace music; two pitch officers south, facing each other.

sentences.zh: 司天監，未後二刻，同郊社令升設昊天上帝、皇地祗神座於壇上北方南向，地祗位在東稍卻，席皆以槁秸。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy, at the second quarter-mark after wei together with the suburban altar director, ascended and set the seats of August Heaven, Supreme Lord and Imperial Earth Sovereign on the altar north facing south; Earth Sovereign's seat east and slightly withdrawn; mats all of straw.
translations.idiomatic: At the second quarter after wei, Astronomy with the suburban altar director set August Heaven and Imperial Earth Sovereign on the altar's north, south-facing; Earth slightly east and withdrawn—straw mats.

sentences.zh: 太祖配位座于東方西向，席以蒲越。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor's paired seat stood east facing west; mat of rush with coarse weave.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor's paired seat stood east, west-facing—rush mat with coarse border.

sentences.zh: 五方帝、日、月、神州地祗、天皇大帝、北極神座於壇上第一等，席皆槁秸，內官五十四座、五神、五官、嶽鎮海瀆二十九座於壇上第二等，中官一百五十有八座、昆侖、山林川澤二十一座於壇上第三等，外官一百六座、丘陵墳衍原隰三十座於內濆之內，眾星三百六十座在內濆之外，席皆以莞。

translations.literal: The Five Directional Emperors, Sun, Moon, Spirit Land of the Realm, August Emperor of Heaven, and North Pole spirit seats on the altar's first tier—all straw mats; fifty-four inner-official seats, five spirits and five officials, twenty-nine seats of peaks, rivers, and seas on the second tier; one hundred fifty-eight middle-official seats, Kunlun and mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes twenty-one seats on the third tier; one hundred six outer-official seats, hills, mounds, tombs, plains, and wetlands thirty seats inside the inner sacred enclosure; three hundred sixty star seats outside the inner sacred enclosure—all rush mats; spirit name tablets each set at the seat head.
translations.idiomatic: Five Directional Emperors, Sun, Moon, Spirit Land, August Emperor of Heaven, and North Pole on the first tier—straw mats; fifty-four inner officials, five spirits and five officials, twenty-nine peaks and seas on the second; one hundred fifty-eight middle officials, Kunlun and landwaters twenty-one on the third; one hundred six outer officials, hills and wetlands thirty inside the inner enclosure; three hundred sixty stars outside—all rush mats; name tablets at each head.

sentences.zh: 神座版各設於座首。

translations.literal: Spirit seat tablets were each set at the head of the seat.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit tablets stood at the head of each seat.

sentences.zh: 又設禮神玉。

translations.literal: They also set the ritual jades for the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: They also set the ritual jades for the spirits.

sentences.zh: 俟告潔畢，權徹去壇上及第一等神位，祀日醜前五刻重設。

translations.literal: When the announcement of purity was finished, they temporarily removed the altar-top and first-tier spirit positions; at the fifth quarter-mark before chou on the sacrifice day they were reset.
translations.idiomatic: After the purity announcement, altar-top and first-tier seats were temporarily removed; at the fifth quarter before chou on sacrifice day they were reset.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎同司尊及執事者設天、地、配位各左十有一籩，右十有一豆，俱為三行。

translations.literal: The ritual attendant together with the vessel keeper and executives set for Heaven, Earth, and the paired seat each left eleven platters, right eleven bowls, all in three rows.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant, vessel keeper, and executives set Heaven, Earth, and the paired seat each with eleven platters left, eleven bowls right, three rows.

sentences.zh: 登三在籩豆間。

translations.literal: Three ascent vessels stood between platters and bowls.
translations.idiomatic: Three ascent vessels between platters and bowls.

sentences.zh: 簠一簋一於登前，簠在左，簋在右。

translations.literal: One grain vessel and one millet vessel before the ascent vessels; grain vessel left, millet vessel right.
translations.idiomatic: One grain vessel and one millet vessel before the ascent vessels—grain left, millet right.

sentences.zh: 各於神座前藉以席。

translations.literal: Each before its spirit seat, spread with mats.
translations.idiomatic: Each before its spirit seat on spread mats.

sentences.zh: 又設天、地位太尊各二、著尊各二、犧尊各二，山罍各二，壇上東南隅配位著尊二、犧尊二、象奠二，在天、地位酒尊之東，俱北向西上，皆有坫，加勺、冪，為酌尊所。

translations.literal: They also set for Heaven and Earth positions each two Grand Vessels, two Display Vessels, two Sacrificial Vessels, two Mountain Vessels; for the paired seat at the altar's southeast corner two Display Vessels, two Sacrificial Vessels, two Elephant Offerings, east of the Heaven and Earth wine vessels, all north-facing west-upper, each with stand, ladle, and cover—as libation stations.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth each received two Grand, Display, Sacrificial, and Mountain Vessels; the paired seat at the southeast corner two Display, two Sacrificial, two Elephant Offerings east of the Heaven and Earth wine vessels—north-facing west-upper, stands, ladles, covers—as libation stations.

sentences.zh: 又天、地位象尊各二、壺尊各二、山罍各四，在壇下午陛之南，北向西上。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth positions also each two Elephant Vessels, two Jar Vessels, four Mountain Vessels south of the wu steps below the altar, north-facing west-upper.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth also each two Elephant Vessels, two Jar Vessels, four Mountain Vessels south of the wu steps below the altar, north-facing west-upper.

sentences.zh: 配位壺尊二、山罍四在酉陛之北，東向北上，皆有坫，設而不酌，亦左以明水，右以玄酒。

translations.literal: Paired seat Jar Vessels two, Mountain Vessels four north of the you steps, east-facing north-upper, all with stands, set but not poured—left clear water, right dark wine.
translations.idiomatic: Paired seat: two Jar Vessels, four Mountain Vessels north of the you steps, east-facing north-upper—with stands, set but not poured; left clear water, right dark wine.

sentences.zh: 又設五方帝、日、月、神州地祗、天皇大帝、北極，第一等皆左八籩、右八豆，登在籩豆間，簠一簋一在登前，爵坫一在神座前。

translations.literal: They also set the Five Directional Emperors, Sun, Moon, Spirit Land, August Emperor of Heaven, and North Pole on the first tier—each left eight platters, right eight bowls, ascent between platters and bowls, one grain and one millet vessel before ascent, one libation stand before the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: Five Directional Emperors, Sun, Moon, Spirit Land, August Emperor, and North Pole on the first tier—each eight platters left, eight bowls right, ascent between, grain and millet before ascent, libation stand before the seat.

sentences.zh: 第二等內官五十四座，五神、五官、嶽鎮海瀆二十九座，每座邊二、豆二、簠一、簋二、俎一、爵坫一。

translations.literal: Second tier: fifty-four inner-official seats, five spirits and five officials, twenty-nine peaks and seas—each seat two platters, two bowls, one grain vessel, two millet vessels, one meat stand, one libation stand.
translations.idiomatic: Second tier: fifty-four inner officials, five spirits and officials, twenty-nine peaks and seas—each two platters, two bowls, one grain vessel, two millet vessels, one meat stand, one libation stand.

sentences.zh: 第三等中官一百五十八座，昆侖、山林川澤二十一座，及內濆內外官一百六座，丘陵墳衍原隰三十座，內濆外眾星三百六十座，每位籩二、豆二、簠一、簋一、俎一、爵一。

translations.literal: Third tier: one hundred fifty-eight middle-official seats, Kunlun and landwaters twenty-one, plus one hundred six outer officials inside and outside the inner enclosure, hills and wetlands thirty, three hundred sixty stars outside the inner enclosure—each two platters, two bowls, one grain vessel, one millet vessel, one meat stand, one libation cup.
translations.idiomatic: Third tier: one hundred fifty-eight middle officials, twenty-one Kunlun and landwaters, one hundred six outer officials, thirty hills and wetlands, three hundred sixty stars—each two platters, two bowls, grain and millet vessels, meat stand, libation cup.

sentences.zh: 又設第一等每位太尊二、著尊二、皆有坫加勺。

translations.literal: They also set for each first-tier seat two Grand Vessels and two Display Vessels, all with stands and ladles.
translations.idiomatic: Each first-tier seat also two Grand and two Display Vessels—with stands and ladles.

sentences.zh: 第二等每陛山尊二，第三等每位蜃尊二，內濆內外每辰概尊二，皆加勺。

translations.literal: Second tier: two Mountain Vessels per step; third tier: two Clam Vessels each; inside and outside the inner enclosure two General Vessels per chen station—all with ladles.
translations.idiomatic: Second tier: two Mountain Vessels per step; third tier: two Clam Vessels each; inner and outer enclosure two General Vessels per chen—all ladled.

sentences.zh: 自第二等已下皆用匏爵，先洗拭訖，置於尊所，其尊所皆在神位之左。

translations.literal: From the second tier down all used gourd libation cups; washed and wiped first, then placed at the vessel station; vessel stations all lay left of the spirit position.
translations.idiomatic: From the second tier down, gourd cups—washed, wiped, placed at the vessel station left of each spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 凡祭器皆藉以席，籩豆各加巾蓋。

translations.literal: All sacrificial vessels were spread with mats; platters and bowls each covered with cloth.
translations.idiomatic: All vessels on mats; platters and bowls under cloth covers.

sentences.zh: 又設天、地及配位籩一、豆一、簠一、簋一、俎四、及毛血豆各一，並第一等神位每位俎二，於饌幔內。

translations.literal: They also set for Heaven, Earth, and the paired seat one platter, one bowl, one grain vessel, one millet vessel, four meat stands, and one raw-blood bowl each; and for each first-tier spirit seat two meat stands—in the offering canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, Earth, and paired seat each one platter, bowl, grain and millet vessel, four meat stands, one raw-blood bowl; each first-tier seat two meat stands—in the offering canopy.

sentences.zh: 又設皇帝洗位於卯陛下，道北，南向。

translations.literal: They also set the Emperor's washing station north of the mao steps below, path north, south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's washing station stood north of the mao steps below, path north, south-facing.

sentences.zh: 盥洗在東，爵洗在西。

translations.literal: Hand-washing east; libation-washing west.
translations.idiomatic: Hand-washing east; libation-washing west.

sentences.zh: 匜在東，巾在西。

translations.literal: Pouring vessel east; towel west.
translations.idiomatic: Pouring vessel east; towel west.

sentences.zh: 篚南肆，實玉爵坫。

translations.literal: Basket spread south, holding jade libation stand.
translations.idiomatic: Basket spread south, holding the jade libation stand.

sentences.zh: 又設亞終獻洗位在小次之東，南向。

translations.literal: They also set the secondary and final offering washing station east of the lesser pavilion, south-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Secondary and final offering washing stood east of the lesser pavilion, south-facing.

sentences.zh: 盥洗在東，爵洗在西，加勺。

translations.literal: Hand-washing east; libation-washing west, with ladle.
translations.idiomatic: Hand-washing east; libation-washing west, with ladle.

sentences.zh: 篚在西，南肆，加巾。

translations.literal: Basket west, spread south, with cloth cover.
translations.idiomatic: Basket west, spread south, with cloth cover.

sentences.zh: 又設第一等分獻官盥洗爵洗位，及第二等分獻官盥洗位，各於其辰陛道之左，罍在洗左，篚在洗右，俱內向，執罍篚者位於其後。

translations.literal: They also set first-tier divided offering officials' hand-washing and libation-washing stations, and second-tier divided offering officials' hand-washing stations, each on the left of its chen step path; jar left of washing, basket right of washing, both inward-facing; jar and basket holders behind.
translations.idiomatic: First-tier divided offerers: hand-washing and libation-washing left of each chen step; second-tier: hand-washing only—jar left of wash, basket right, inward-facing; holders behind.

sentences.zh: 太府監、少府監祀前一日未後二刻，帥其屬升壇陳玉幣。

translations.literal: The Imperial Store director and Palace Workshops director, at the second quarter-mark after wei on the day before sacrifice, led their subordinates up the altar to display jade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: At the second quarter after wei the day before sacrifice, Imperial Store and Palace Workshops directors led their staffs up to display jade and silk.

sentences.zh: 昊天上帝以蒼壁、蒼幣，皇地祗以黃琮、黃幣，配位以蒼幣，黃帝以黃琮，青帝以青珪，赤帝以赤璋，大明以青珪璧，白帝以白琥，黑帝以玄璜，北極以青珪璧，天皇大帝以玄珪璧，神州地祗以玄色兩珪有邸，皆置於匣。

translations.literal: August Heaven, Supreme Lord used dark green disk and dark green silk; Imperial Earth Sovereign used yellow regalia and yellow silk; paired seat used dark green silk; Yellow Emperor used yellow regalia; Green Emperor used green tablet; Red Emperor used red regalia; Great Brightness used green tablet-disk; White Emperor used white regalia; Black Emperor used dark regalia; North Pole used green tablet-disk; August Emperor of Heaven used dark tablet-disk; Spirit Land of the Realm used two dark tablets with base—all placed in cases.
translations.idiomatic: August Heaven: dark green disk and silk. Earth Sovereign: yellow regalia and silk. Paired seat: dark green silk. Yellow Emperor: yellow regalia. Green Emperor: green tablet. Red Emperor: red regalia. Great Brightness: green tablet-disk. White Emperor: white regalia. Black Emperor: dark regalia. North Pole: green tablet-disk. August Emperor of Heaven: dark tablet-disk. Spirit Land: two dark tablets with base—all cased.

sentences.zh: 五帝之幣各從其方色。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors' silk each followed its directional color.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors' silk followed each direction's color.

sentences.zh: 凡幣皆陳於篚。

translations.literal: All silk was displayed in baskets.
translations.idiomatic: All silk lay in baskets.

sentences.zh: 設訖，俟告潔訖權徹去，祀日重設。

translations.literal: When setting was finished, after the purity announcement they were temporarily removed; on the sacrifice day they were reset.
translations.idiomatic: When set, they were removed after the purity announcement and reset on sacrifice day.

sentences.zh: 祀日醜前五刻，禮部設祝冊神座之右，皆藉以案。

translations.literal: At the fifth quarter-mark before chou on the sacrifice day, the Ministry of Rites set invocation tablets right of the spirit seats, all on tables.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth quarter before chou, Rites set invocation tablets right of the seats, on tables.

sentences.zh: 太常卿明燈燎。

translations.literal: The Director of Grand Harmony lit the fire-pit lamps.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Grand Harmony lit the fire-pit lamps.

sentences.zh: 戶部郎中設諸州歲貢于宮縣東北，金為前列，玉帛次之，餘為從列，皆藉以席，立于歲貢之後，北向。

translations.literal: The Revenue Bureau director set each circuit's annual tribute northeast of the palace music—gold foremost, silk and jade after, the rest in trailing rows, all on mats, standing behind the tribute, north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue set annual tribute northeast of palace music—gold first, silk and jade next, the rest behind—all on mats, north-facing behind the rows.

sentences.zh: 太府監、少府監設異寶嘉瑞于宮縣西，北上，瑞居前，中下次之，皆藉以席，立於實後，北向。

translations.literal: Imperial Store and Palace Workshops directors set exotic treasures and auspicious omens west of the palace music, north-upper—omens before, middling and lesser after—all on mats, standing behind the treasures, north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Store and Palace Workshops set treasures and omens west of palace music, north-upper—omens first, middling and lesser after—on mats, north-facing behind.

sentences.zh: 少府少監設伐國毀寶于宮縣東南，皆藉以席，立於寶後，北向。

translations.literal: The Palace Workshops vice director set spoils of conquered states southeast of the palace music, all on mats, standing behind the treasures, north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Workshops vice director set conquered spoils southeast—on mats, north-facing behind.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎設八寶于宮縣西南，各分立于寶南，皆北向。

translations.literal: Seal officers set the eight treasures southwest of the palace music, each divided south of its treasure, all north-facing.
translations.idiomatic: Seal officers set the eight treasures southwest—each south of its treasure, north-facing.

sentences.zh: 司天監、太府監、少府監、郊社令、奉禮郎升設昊天上帝、皇地祗、配位、及壇上第一等神座，又設玉幣，各於其位。

translations.literal: Astronomy, Imperial Store, Palace Workshops, suburban altar director, and ritual attendant ascended and set August Heaven, Imperial Earth Sovereign, paired seat, and first-tier spirit seats, and also set jade and silk at each position.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomy, Imperial Store, Palace Workshops, suburban altar director, and attendants reset Heaven, Earth, paired seat, and first-tier seats with jade and silk at each post.

sentences.zh: 太祝取瘞玉加於幣，以禮神之玉各置於神座前，乃退。

translations.literal: The grand invoker took burying jade and added it to the silk; the ritual jades for the spirits were each placed before the spirit seat, then they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The grand invoker added burying jade to the silk, placed each ritual jade before its seat, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿帥其屬入實祭器。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Victuals led his subordinates to fill the sacrificial vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Victuals filled the sacrificial vessels.

sentences.zh: 昊天上帝、皇地祇、配位每位籩三行，以右為上，形鹽在前，魚鱐糗餌次之，第二行榛實在前，乾桃乾裛乾棗次之，第三行乾菱在前，乾芡乾栗鹿脯次之。

translations.literal: August Heaven, Supreme Lord, Imperial Earth Sovereign, and paired seat each three rows of platters—right as upper; shaped salt foremost, fish, dried meat, and pounded cakes after; second row hazelnut foremost, dried peach, dried meat-strip, dried jujube after; third row dried water-caltrop foremost, dried gorgon, dried chestnut, and deer jerky after.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, Earth, and paired seat: three platter rows—right upper; shaped salt first, then fish, dried meat, pounded cakes; second row hazelnut, dried peach, meat-strip, jujube; third row water-caltrop, gorgon, chestnut, deer jerky.

sentences.zh: 豆三行，以左為上，芹菹在前，筍菹葵菹次之，第二行韭菹在前，菁菹魚醢兔醢次之，第三行豚胉在前，醓醢酏食鹿臡次之。

translations.literal: Three rows of bowls—left as upper; celery pickle foremost, bamboo-shoot, sunflower, and vegetable pickles after; second row leek pickle foremost, smartweed pickle, fish paste, rabbit paste after; third row suckling-pig foremost, fermented paste, thick sauce, deer hash after.
translations.idiomatic: Three bowl rows—left upper; celery pickle, bamboo-shoot and vegetable pickles; leek, smartweed, fish and rabbit paste; suckling-pig, fermented paste, thick sauce, deer hash.

sentences.zh: 簠黍，簋稷，登皆大羹。

translations.literal: Grain vessel millet, millet vessel grain; ascent vessels all great broth.
translations.idiomatic: Grain vessel: millet; millet vessel: grain; ascent vessels: great broth.

sentences.zh: 第一等壇上一十位，每位皆實籩三行，以右為上，形鹽在前，魚鱐次之，第二行乾裛在前，桃棗次之，第三行乾芡在前，榛實鹿脯次之。

translations.literal: First tier on the altar, ten seats—each three platter rows, right upper; shaped salt foremost, fish and dried meat after; second row dried meat-strip foremost, peach and jujube after; third row dried gorgon foremost, hazelnut and deer jerky after.
translations.idiomatic: First tier, ten seats: three platter rows—right upper; salt, fish, dried meat; meat-strip, peach, jujube; gorgon, hazelnut, deer jerky.

sentences.zh: 豆三行以左為上，芹菹在前，筍菹次之，第二行菁菹在前，韭菹魚醢次之，第三行豚胉在前，醓醢鹿臡次之。

translations.literal: Three bowl rows, left upper; celery pickle foremost, bamboo-shoot after; second row smartweed foremost, leek and fish paste after; third row suckling-pig foremost, fermented paste and deer hash after.
translations.idiomatic: Three bowl rows—left upper; celery, bamboo-shoot; smartweed, leek, fish paste; suckling-pig, fermented paste, deer hash.

sentences.zh: 簠黍，簋稷，登大羹，第二、第三等每位籩二，鹿脯、乾棗。

translations.literal: Grain vessel millet, millet vessel grain, ascent great broth; second and third tier each two platters—deer jerky, dried jujube.
translations.idiomatic: Grain and millet vessels, ascent great broth; second and third tier: two platters each—deer jerky, dried jujube.

sentences.zh: 豆二，鹿臡、菁菹。

translations.literal: Two bowls—deer hash, smartweed pickle.
translations.idiomatic: Two bowls: deer hash, smartweed pickle.

sentences.zh: 俎，羊一段。

translations.literal: Meat stand: one section of sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Meat stand: one section of sheep.

sentences.zh: 內濆內、內濆外每位籩鹿脯，豆鹿臡，俎羊一段。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the inner enclosure each: platter deer jerky, bowl deer hash, meat stand one section of sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the inner enclosure: platter deer jerky, bowl deer hash, one sheep section on the stand.

sentences.zh: 良醖令帥其屬入實尊罍，昊天上帝、皇地祇大尊為上，實以泛齊；

translations.literal: The chief brewer led his subordinates to fill the wine vessels; for August Heaven and Imperial Earth Sovereign the Grand Vessel was uppermost, filled with first-ferment wine;
translations.idiomatic: The chief brewer filled the wine vessels; for August Heaven and Imperial Earth Sovereign the Grand Vessel stood highest, filled with first-ferment wine;

sentences.zh: 著尊次之，實以醴齊；

translations.literal: the Display Vessel next, filled with sweet wine;
translations.idiomatic: the Display Vessel next, filled with sweet wine;

sentences.zh: 犧尊次之，實以盎齊；

translations.literal: The sacrificial bronzes came next, filled with ang-ferment;
translations.idiomatic: Next the sacrificial bronzes, filled with ang-ferment;

sentences.zh: 壺尊次之，實以醍齊，象尊次之；

translations.literal: the hu bronzes next, filled with ti-ferment; the elephant bronzes next;
translations.idiomatic: then the hu bronzes with ti-ferment; then the elephant bronzes;

sentences.zh: 實以沈齊，山罍為下，實以三酒。

translations.literal: filled with chen-ferment; the mountain lei were lowest, filled with the three wines.
translations.idiomatic: filled with chen-ferment; the mountain lei last, filled with the three wines.

sentences.zh: 配位著尊為上，實以泛齊；

translations.literal: For the associated positions the zhuo bronzes were uppermost, filled with wan-ferment;
translations.idiomatic: At the associated positions the zhuo bronzes ranked first, filled with wan-ferment;

sentences.zh: 犧尊次之，實以醴齊；

translations.literal: the sacrificial bronzes next, filled with li-ferment;
translations.idiomatic: the sacrificial bronzes next with li-ferment;

sentences.zh: 象尊次之，實以盎齊；

translations.literal: the elephant bronzes next, filled with ang-ferment;
translations.idiomatic: the elephant bronzes next with ang-ferment;

sentences.zh: 壺尊次之，實以醍齊；

translations.literal: the hu bronzes next, filled with ti-ferment;
translations.idiomatic: the hu bronzes next with ti-ferment;

sentences.zh: 山罍為下，實以三酒。

translations.literal: the mountain lei were lowest, filled with the three wines.
translations.idiomatic: the mountain lei last, filled with the three wines.

sentences.zh: 第一等每位大尊實以泛齊，著尊實以醴齊。

translations.literal: First rank, each position: the great bronzes filled with wan-ferment, the zhuo bronzes with li-ferment.
translations.idiomatic: First rank at each seat: great bronzes with wan-ferment, zhuo bronzes with li-ferment.

sentences.zh: 第二等山尊實以醍齊。

translations.literal: Second rank: mountain bronzes filled with ti-ferment.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank: mountain bronzes with ti-ferment.

sentences.zh: 第三等及內濆內，蜃尊實以泛齊。

translations.literal: Third rank and within the inner enclosure, clam bronzes filled with wan-ferment.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and inside the inner enclosure: clam bronzes with wan-ferment.

sentences.zh: 內濆外及眾星，概尊實以三酒。

translations.literal: Outside the inner enclosure and the host of stars, gai bronzes filled with the three wines.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the inner enclosure and the stars: gai bronzes with the three wines.

sentences.zh: 省牲器：祀前一日午後八刻，去壇二百步禁止行人。

translations.literal: Inspecting the victim vessels: on the day before the sacrifice, at the eighth quarter after noon, within two hundred paces of the altar foot-traffic was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting the victim vessels: the eve of sacrifice, eighth quarter after noon, no one might pass within two hundred paces of the altar.

sentences.zh: 未後二刻，郊社令丞帥其屬掃除壇之上下，司尊、奉禮郎帥執事者以祭器入，設於位。

translations.literal: At the second quarter of wei, the suburban-altar director and assistants led their staff to sweep above and below the altar; the director of vessels and presentation officers led the attendants to bring in the ritual vessels and set them at their stations.
translations.idiomatic: At the second wei quarter the suburban-altar director swept the altar; vessel directors and presentation officers brought the ritual gear to its stations.

sentences.zh: 司天監設神位，太府監、少府監陳玉幣於篚。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy set out the spirit tablets; the Grand and Junior Treasuries laid jade and silks in baskets.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomy set the spirit tablets; the treasuries laid out jade and silk in baskets.

sentences.zh: 未後三刻，禮直官引廩犧令與諸太祝、祝史以牲就位。

translations.literal: At the third quarter of wei, ritual orderlies led the director of sacrificial livestock with the grand invokers and invoker scribes to bring the victims into place.
translations.idiomatic: Third wei quarter: orderlies led the livestock director, grand invokers, and scribes to position the victims.

sentences.zh: 又禮直官贊者分引禮部尚書、太常卿、光祿卿、禮部侍郎、太常丞、監祭御史、監禮博士、廩犧令，太官令、太官丞詣內濆東門外省牲位。

translations.literal: Again orderlies and presenters in turn led the Minister of Rites, Director of Imperial Sacrifices, Director of Imperial Banquets, Vice Minister of Rites, Vice Director of Sacrifices, supervising censor, supervising ritual academic, director of sacrificial livestock, Director of the Imperial Kitchen, and kitchen assistants to the outer victim station east of the inner-enclosure gate.
translations.idiomatic: Presenters then led the Minister of Rites, sacrifice and banquet directors, vice ministers, supervising censor and ritual academic, livestock director, kitchen director and aides to the outer victim pen east of the inner gate.

sentences.zh: 立定，乃引禮部尚書、侍郎、太常丞、及監祭御史、監禮博士升自卯階，視濯滌，執事者皆舉冪告潔，俱畢，降復位。

translations.literal: When all stood, they led the Minister, vice minister, vice director, supervising censor, and ritual academic up the mao stair to inspect washing; attendants all raised covers and announced purity—when finished they descended and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Once formed up, the Minister, vice minister, vice director, censor, and academic climbed the mao stair to inspect the washing; attendants lifted covers and cried "pure"—then all descended.

sentences.zh: 禮直官稍前曰：「告潔畢，請省牲。

translations.literal: A ritual orderly stepped forward and said: "Purity announced complete—please inspect the victims."
translations.idiomatic: An orderly announced: "Purity complete—inspect the victims."

sentences.zh: 」禮部尚書侍郎及太常卿丞稍前，省牲訖，退，復位。

translations.literal: The Minister, vice minister, and Director of Sacrifices and vice director stepped forward, inspected the victims, withdrew, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister, vice minister, and sacrifice directors inspected the victims and returned.

sentences.zh: 次引光祿卿丞巡牲一匝，光祿卿退，光祿丞西向折身曰：「備訖。

translations.literal: Next they led the Director of Banquets and assistant to make one circuit of the victims; the director withdrew, and the assistant, facing west, bowed at the waist and said: "Preparations complete."
translations.idiomatic: The banquet director and aide circled the victims; the director withdrew, the aide faced west, bowed, and said: "Ready."

sentences.zh: 」乃復位。

translations.literal: Then they returned to station.
translations.idiomatic: Then all resumed their places.

sentences.zh: 次引廩犧令巡牲一匝，西向躬身曰：「充。

translations.literal: Next they led the director of sacrificial livestock on one circuit; facing west he bowed and said: "Sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: The livestock director circled once, faced west, bowed, and said: "Sufficient."

sentences.zh: 」又引諸祝史巡牲一匝，首一員西向躬身曰：「腯。

translations.literal: Again they led the invoker scribes on one circuit; the lead scribe, facing west, bowed and said: "Plump."
translations.idiomatic: Invoker scribes circled; the lead, facing west, bowed and said: "Plump."

sentences.zh: 」畢，俱復位。

translations.literal: When finished, all returned.
translations.idiomatic: Done, all returned.

sentences.zh: 禮直官稍前曰：「請省饌。

translations.literal: A ritual orderly stepped forward and said: "Please inspect the offerings."
translations.idiomatic: An orderly said: "Inspect the offerings."

sentences.zh: 」乃引禮部尚書以下各就位，立定，省饌，訖，禮直官引禮部尚書侍郎、太常卿丞各還齋所，餘官廩犧令與諸太祝祝史以次牽牲詣廚，授太官令丞。

translations.literal: They then led the Minister of Rites and the rest each to his station; when set they inspected the offerings. When finished, orderlies led the Minister and vice minister and Director and vice director back to the fasting lodges; the remaining officers—the livestock director with grand invokers and scribes—in turn led the victims to the kitchen and handed them to the kitchen director and assistants.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister and others inspected the offerings, then the Minister, vice minister, and sacrifice directors returned to the fast-lodges while the livestock director and invokers led the victims to the kitchen.

sentences.zh: 次引光祿卿丞、監祭、監禮詣廚，省鼎鑊，視滌濯畢，乃還齋所。

translations.literal: Next they led the banquet director and assistant, supervising censor, and supervising ritual academic to the kitchen to inspect cauldrons and washing; when finished they returned to the fast-lodges.
translations.idiomatic: The banquet officers, censor, and academic inspected kitchen cauldrons and washing, then returned to fast.

sentences.zh: 晡後一刻，太官令帥宰人以鸞刀割牲，祝史各取毛血實以豆，置於饌幔，遂烹牲，祝史乃取瘞血貯於盤。

translations.literal: At the first quarter after the shen hour the kitchen director led butchers with the phoenix knife to cut the victims; invoker scribes each took blood and hair in a dou and set them at the offering curtain, then cooked the victims; the scribes then stored the buried blood in a tray.
translations.idiomatic: First shen quarter: the kitchen director's butchers cut the victims; scribes took blood and hair in dous for the offering curtain, then cooked the meat and set burial blood in trays.

sentences.zh: 奠玉幣：祀日醜前五刻，亞終獻司徒已下，應行事陪從群官，各服其服就次。

translations.literal: Presenting jade and silk: on the sacrifice day, five quarters before the chou hour, the secondary and final offerers, the Minister of Education downward, and all attendant officials took their robes and went to their stations.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting jade and silk: five quarters before chou on sacrifice day, secondary and final offerers, the Minister of Education, and all attendant officers robed and took station.

sentences.zh: 司天監複設壇上及第一等神位。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy again set out the altar and first-rank spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomy again set the altar and first-rank tablets.

sentences.zh: 太府監、少府監陳玉幣。

translations.literal: The Grand and Junior Treasuries laid out jade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The treasuries laid out jade and silk.

sentences.zh: 太常卿、郊社令丞明燭燎。

translations.literal: The Director of Sacrifices and suburban-altar directors lit the torches.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrifice director and suburban-altar officers lit the torches.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿丞實籩豆簠簋尊罍，俟監祭、監禮案視訖，徹去巾蓋。

translations.literal: The banquet director and assistant filled baskets, dous, grain vessels, and wine vessels; when the supervising censor and academic had inspected, the cloth covers were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet officers filled baskets, dous, grain vessels, and wine jars; after censor and academic inspection the covers came off.

sentences.zh: 大樂令帥工人布于宮縣之內、文舞八佾立於縣前表後，武舞八佾各為四佾立于宮縣左右，引舞執纛等在前，又引登歌樂工由卯陛而升，各就其位。

translations.literal: The Director of Music led artisans to deploy within the palace bells; eight rows of civil dancers stood before the bell-frame table; eight rows of martial dancers, four each, stood left and right of the bells; dance captains with banners went before; then singing musicians ascended by the mao stair to their places.
translations.idiomatic: The music director arrayed players within the palace bells; eight civil dance rows before the frame, martial dancers in fours to either side; captains with banners led; singing musicians climbed the mao stair to station.

sentences.zh: 歌、擊、彈者坐，吹者立。

translations.literal: Singers, strikers, and pluckers sat; pipers stood.
translations.idiomatic: Singers, strikers, and pluckers sat; pipers stood.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎贊者先入就位，餘禮直官、贊者分引分獻宮，監祭御史、監禮博士、諸執事及太祝、祝史、齋郎、助奠、執尊罍、舉冪等官，入自中壝東門，當壇南重行西上、北向立定。

translations.literal: Presentation officers and presenters entered first; other orderlies and presenters in turn led the distributed-offering princes, supervising censor and academic, all attendants, grand invokers, scribe invokers, fast-officers, assistants, vessel-bearers, and cover-lifters in through the central-enclosure east gate, double-ranked west of the altar facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Presentation officers entered first; orderlies led distributed-offering lords, censor, academic, invokers, fast-officers, assistants, and vessel-bearers through the central east gate, double-ranked west of the altar facing north.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎贊：「拜。

translations.literal: A presentation officer called: "Bow."
translations.idiomatic: A presenter called: "Bow."

sentences.zh: 」分獻官以下皆再拜，訖，奉禮贊曰：「各就位。

translations.literal: Distributed-offering officers and below all bowed twice; when finished the presenter said: "Each to his station."
translations.idiomatic: Distributed offerers and below bowed twice; then "Each to his station."

sentences.zh: 」贊者、禮直官分引監祭御史、監禮博士，按視壇之上下，糾察不如儀者，退復位。

translations.literal: Presenters and orderlies in turn led the supervising censor and academic to inspect above and below the altar, correct improprieties, and return.
translations.idiomatic: Presenters led censor and academic to inspect the altar, correct lapses, and return.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引司徒入就位，西向立。

translations.literal: An orderly led the Minister of Education to his station, standing west.
translations.idiomatic: An orderly led the Minister of Education west to his station.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引博士，博士引亞獻，自東濆偏門人就位，西向立。

translations.literal: An orderly led the academic; the academic led the secondary offerer through the east-enclosure side gate to station, standing west.
translations.idiomatic: An orderly led the academic, who led the secondary offerer in by the east side gate to stand west.

sentences.zh: 又禮直官引終獻，次於其位。

translations.literal: Again an orderly led the final offerer to station after him.
translations.idiomatic: Another orderly placed the final offerer next in line.

sentences.zh: 祀日未明一刻，通事舍人引侍中詣齋殿，跪奏：「請中嚴。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day, one quarter before dawn, the communications officer led the attendant-in-waiting to the fast-palace, who knelt and reported: "Please sound the middle vigil."
translations.idiomatic: One quarter before dawn the communications officer brought the attendant-in-waiting to the fast-palace to kneel and report: "Sound the middle vigil."

sentences.zh: 」俯伏，興。

translations.literal: He bowed prostrate and rose.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated and rose.

sentences.zh: 又少頃，乃跪奏：「外辦。

translations.literal: After a little while he knelt again and reported: "The outer rites are ready."
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he knelt again: "The outer rites are ready."

sentences.zh: 」俟尚輦進輿，乃跪奏稱：「具官臣某，請皇帝降座升輿」。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was brought forward he knelt and said: "Your subject [name] requests that Your Majesty descend and mount the carriage."
translations.idiomatic: When the carriage came he knelt: "Your subject [name] asks that Your Majesty descend and mount."

sentences.zh: 皇帝至大次，乃跪奏稱：「具官臣某，請皇帝降輿。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached the great tent he knelt and said: "Your subject [name] requests that Your Majesty descend from the carriage."
translations.idiomatic: At the great tent he knelt: "Your subject [name] asks that Your Majesty alight."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝入次，即位於大次外。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the tent and took station outside the great tent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered and stood outside the great tent.
