sentences.zh: 質明，詣次前跪奏：「請中嚴。

translations.literal: At full dawn he came before the tent, knelt, and reported: "Please sound the middle vigil."
translations.idiomatic: At full dawn he knelt before the tent: "Please sound the middle vigil."

sentences.zh: 」少頃，又奏：「外辦。

translations.literal: After a little while he again reported: "The outer rites are ready."
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he reported again: "The outer rites are ready."

sentences.zh: 」訖，太常卿乃當次前跪稱：「具官臣某，請皇帝行事。

translations.literal: When finished, the Director of Sacrifices knelt before the tent and said: "Your subject [name] requests that Your Majesty perform the rite."
translations.idiomatic: Done, the sacrifice director knelt at the tent: "Your subject [name] asks that Your Majesty perform the rite."

sentences.zh: 」俯伏，興。

translations.literal: He bowed prostrate and rose.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated and rose.

sentences.zh: 凡跪奏，准此。

translations.literal: All kneeling reports followed this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: All kneeling reports followed this form.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出次，乃前導至中濆門，殿中監進大圭，太常卿奏：「請執大圭。

translations.literal: The emperor left the tent; guides went before to the central-enclosure gate; the palace director presented the great jade tablet; the sacrifice director reported: "Please take the great tablet."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left the tent; guides led to the central gate; the palace director presented the great tablet; the sacrifice director said: "Take the great tablet."

sentences.zh: 」入自正門，皇帝入小次位，西向立，太常卿乃與博士分左右立定，乃奏：「有司謹具，請行事。

translations.literal: Entering by the main gate, the emperor entered the small tent facing west; the sacrifice director and academic stood left and right; he reported: "The officers have prepared all—please perform the rite."
translations.idiomatic: Through the main gate the emperor entered the small tent facing west; director and academic flanked him and reported: "All is ready—please proceed."

sentences.zh: 」降神，六成，樂止。

translations.literal: Descent of the spirit: the sixth movement; music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Descent of the spirit: sixth movement; music stopped.

sentences.zh: 太常卿別一員，乃升煙瘞血，訖，乃奏：「拜。

translations.literal: Another sacrifice director ascended to raise smoke and bury the blood; when finished he reported: "Bow."
translations.idiomatic: Another director ascended to raise smoke and bury blood; done, he called: "Bow."

sentences.zh: 」訖，俟侍中升壇，請詣盥洗位。

translations.literal: When finished they waited for the attendant-in-waiting to ascend the altar and request the washing station.
translations.idiomatic: Done, they waited for the attendant to ascend and lead the emperor to wash.

sentences.zh: 至位，奏：「請搢大圭、盥手。

translations.literal: At the station he reported: "Please insert the great tablet and wash the hands."
translations.idiomatic: At the station: "Insert the great tablet and wash the hands."

sentences.zh: 」訖，奏：「請帨手。

translations.literal: When finished he reported: "Please dry the hands."
translations.idiomatic: Done: "Dry the hands."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝帨手，訖，奏：「請執大圭。

translations.literal: The emperor dried his hands; when finished he reported: "Please take the great tablet."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dried his hands; then: "Take the great tablet."

sentences.zh: 」乃引至壇上，殿中監進鎮圭，乃奏：「請搢大圭、執鎮圭。

translations.literal: They then led him to the altar; the palace director presented the securing tablet; he reported: "Please insert the great tablet and take the securing tablet."
translations.idiomatic: They led him up; the palace director gave the securing tablet; "Insert the great tablet and take the securing tablet."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝執鎮圭，詣昊天上帝神座前，奏：「請跪，奠鎮圭。

translations.literal: The emperor took the securing tablet and went before the tablet of Supreme Sovereign of August Heaven; he reported: "Please kneel and set down the securing tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Before August Heaven's tablet he was told: "Kneel and set down the securing tablet."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝奠，訖，執大圭，俯伏，興。

translations.literal: The emperor set it down, took the great tablet, bowed prostrate, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: He set it down, took the great tablet, prostrated, and rose.

sentences.zh: 侍中進玉幣，乃奏：「請搢大圭、跪奠玉幣。

translations.literal: The attendant-in-waiting advanced the jade and silk; he reported: "Please insert the great tablet, kneel, and set down jade and silk."
translations.idiomatic: The attendant brought jade and silk; "Insert the great tablet, kneel, and set down jade and silk."

sentences.zh: 」訖，乃奏：「請執大圭。

translations.literal: When finished he reported: "Please take the great tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Done: "Take the great tablet."

sentences.zh: 」俯伏，興。

translations.literal: He bowed prostrate and rose.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated and rose.

sentences.zh: 少退，又奏：「請再拜。

translations.literal: He withdrew a little; again he reported: "Please bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: He stepped back; then: "Bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」詣皇地祇及配位，奠鎮圭玉幣，並如儀。

translations.literal: He went to Imperial Earth and the associated positions and set down securing tablet and jade and silk—all by the same observances.
translations.idiomatic: At Imperial Earth and the associated seats he set securing tablet and jade and silk by the same rite.

sentences.zh: 配位唯奏請奠鎮圭及幣。

translations.literal: For the associated positions he only reported setting down securing tablet and silk.
translations.idiomatic: At associated positions only securing tablet and silk were announced.

sentences.zh: 奠玉幣畢，皇帝還版位，乃奏：「請還小次、釋大圭。

translations.literal: When jade and silk were finished the emperor returned to the spirit-board station; he reported: "Please return to the small tent and release the great tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Jade and silk done, the emperor returned; "Return to the small tent and release the great tablet."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝入小次，乃立于小次之南稍東，以俟。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the small tent and stood slightly east of its south side to wait.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the small tent and waited slightly east of its south side.

sentences.zh: 皇帝將奠配位之幣也，贊者分引第一等分獻官詣盥洗位，搢笏、盥手、帨手、執笏，各由其陛升，唯不由午陛。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to set silk at the associated positions, presenters in turn led first-rank distributed-offering officers to the washing station—tuck tablets, wash, dry, take tablets—each ascending by his stair, never by the wu stair.
translations.idiomatic: Before silk at associated seats, presenters led first-rank distributed offerers to wash—tablet tucked, hands washed and dried—each up his own stair, never the wu stair.

sentences.zh: 詣神前，搢笏、跪，太祝以玉幣授之，奠訖，俯伏，興。

translations.literal: Before each deity they tucked tablets and knelt; a grand invoker handed jade and silk; when set they bowed prostrate and rose.
translations.idiomatic: At each seat they knelt with tucked tablets; a grand invoker gave jade and silk; they prostrated and rose.

sentences.zh: 再拜，訖，各由本陛降，復位。

translations.literal: They bowed twice; when finished each descended by his stair and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed twice, descended their stairs, and returned.

sentences.zh: 初，分獻將降也，禮直官引諸祝史、齋郎、應助奠者再拜，祝史各奉毛血之豆入，各由其陛升，諸太祝迎取於壇上，奠訖，退立於尊所。

translations.literal: Earlier, as distributed offerers were about to descend, orderlies led invoker scribes, fast-officers, and assistants to bow twice; scribes each bore the blood-and-hair dous in, ascending each by his stair; grand invokers received them on the altar, set them out, and withdrew to stand by the wine stations.
translations.idiomatic: As distributed offerers descended, orderlies led scribes and fast-officers to bow; scribes bore blood-and-hair dous up; grand invokers set them on the altar and stood by the wine.

sentences.zh: 進熟：奠玉幣訖，降還小次。

translations.literal: Presenting the cooked offering: when jade and silk were finished he descended to the small tent.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting the cooked offering: jade and silk done, he returned to the small tent.

sentences.zh: 有司先陳牛鼎三、羊鼎三、豕鼎三、魚鼎三，各在鑊右。

translations.literal: Officers had already set out three ox cauldrons, three sheep cauldrons, three pig cauldrons, and three fish cauldrons, each to the right of its cooking pot.
translations.idiomatic: Officers had set three ox, sheep, pig, and fish cauldrons each, every cauldron to the right of its pot.

sentences.zh: 太官令丞帥進饌者詣廚，以匕升牛羊豕魚，自鑊各實於鼎。

translations.literal: The kitchen director and assistants led offering-bearers to the kitchen; with ladles they lifted ox, sheep, pig, and fish from the pots into the cauldrons.
translations.idiomatic: Kitchen director and aides led bearers to ladle ox, sheep, pig, and fish from pots into cauldrons.

sentences.zh: 牛羊豕皆肩、臂、臑、肫、胳、正脊各一，長脅二，短脅二、代脅二、凡十一體。

translations.literal: Ox, sheep, and pig each had shoulder, arm, shin, rump, rib-flap, and spine one each, two long flanks, two short flanks, two substitute flanks—eleven portions in all.
translations.idiomatic: Ox, sheep, and pig each: shoulder, arm, shin, rump, rib-flap, spine, two long flanks, two short flanks, two substitute flanks—eleven cuts.

sentences.zh: 牛豕皆三十斤，羊十五斤，魚十五頭一十五斤，實訖，冪之。

translations.literal: Ox and pig thirty jin each, sheep fifteen jin, fish fifteen heads totaling fifteen jin; when filled they were covered.
translations.idiomatic: Ox and pig thirty jin each, sheep fifteen, fish fifteen heads totaling fifteen jin; then covered.

sentences.zh: 祝史二人以扃對舉一鼎，牛鼎在前，羊豕次之，魚又次之，有司執匕以從，各陳於每位饌幔位。

translations.literal: Two scribe invokers lifted one cauldron on paired poles—ox cauldron foremost, sheep and pig next, fish last—with officers bearing ladles following; each was set at its offering-curtain station.
translations.idiomatic: Two scribes bore each cauldron on poles—ox first, then sheep and pig, then fish—ladle-bearers following to each offering curtain.

sentences.zh: 從祀壇上第一等五方帝、大明、夜明、天皇大帝、神州地祇、北極，皆羊豕之體並同。

translations.literal: For associated worship on the altar—first rank: Five Emperors, Great Brightness, Night Brightness, Celestial Sovereign, Imperial Earth of the Nine Regions, and North Pole—all sheep and pig portions were the same.
translations.idiomatic: First-rank associated worship—the Five Emperors, sun and moon, Celestial Sovereign, Nine-Regions Earth, North Pole—used the same sheep and pig cuts.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿帥祝史、齋郎、太官令丞各以匕升牛羊豕魚於俎，肩臂臑在上端，肫胳在下端，脊脅在中，魚即橫置，頭在尊位，設去鼎冪。

translations.literal: The banquet director led scribes, fast-officers, and kitchen officers to lift ox, sheep, pig, and fish onto trays—shoulder and arm at the upper end, rump and rib at the lower, spine and flank in the middle; fish lay crosswise with the head toward the wine station; covers were removed from the cauldrons.
translations.idiomatic: The banquet director led officers to load trays—shoulder and arm above, rump and rib below, spine and flank between; fish crosswise, head toward the wine; cauldron covers off.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿丞同太官令丞實籩豆簠簋，籩實以粉餈，豆實以糝食，簠實稻，簋實粱。

translations.literal: Banquet director and assistant with kitchen director filled baskets and dous and grain vessels—baskets with powdered cakes, dous with grain mash, grain vessel with millet, covered vessel with glutinous millet.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet and kitchen officers filled baskets with powdered cakes, dous with mash, one vessel with millet, one with glutinous grain.

sentences.zh: 俟皇帝還小次，樂止。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the small tent, music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was back in the small tent, music stopped.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引司徒出詣饌幔所，與薦籩豆簠簋俎齋，各奉天、地、配位之饌。

translations.literal: An orderly led the Minister of Education out to the offering curtain with fast-officers bearing baskets, dous, vessels, and trays, each carrying Heaven, Earth, and associated offerings.
translations.idiomatic: An orderly led the Minister of Education to the curtain with fast-officers bearing Heaven, Earth, and associated offerings.

sentences.zh: 司徒帥太官令以序入內濆正門，樂作，至壇下，俟。

translations.literal: The Minister led the kitchen director in order through the inner-enclosure main gate; music played; at the foot of the altar they waited.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister led the kitchen director through the inner main gate with music to the altar foot and waited.

sentences.zh: 祝史進徹毛血豆，降自卯陛，以次出，訖，司徒與薦籩豆簠簋俎齋郎，奉昊天上帝、皇地祇之饌，升自午陛。

translations.literal: Scribe invokers advanced to remove the blood-and-hair dous and descended by the mao stair in order and went out; when finished the Minister and fast-officers bearing August Heaven and Imperial Earth offerings ascended by the wu stair.
translations.idiomatic: Scribes removed the blood dous and left by the mao stair; then the Minister and fast-officers bore Heaven and Earth offerings up the wu stair.

sentences.zh: 太官令丞與薦籩豆簠簋俎齊郎，奉配位及第一等神位之饌，升自卯陛。

translations.literal: Kitchen director and assistants with fast-officers bore associated and first-rank offerings up the mao stair.
translations.idiomatic: Kitchen director and fast-officers bore associated and first-rank offerings up the mao stair.

sentences.zh: 各位太祝迎於壇陛之道間。

translations.literal: At each seat a grand invoker met them on the stair path.
translations.idiomatic: A grand invoker met each party on the stair path.

sentences.zh: 于昊天上帝位，司徒搢笏北向跪奉，粉餈籩在糗餌之前，糝食豆在醓醢之前，簠左簋右，皆在登前，牛俎在豆前，羊豕魚俎次之，以右為上。

translations.literal: At August Heaven's station the Minister tucked his tablet, knelt north, and presented—the powdered-cake basket before the grain cake, the mash dou before the fermented dou, grain vessel left and covered vessel right, both before the grand stew, ox tray before the dous, sheep, pig, and fish trays after, right ranking uppermost.
translations.idiomatic: At August Heaven the Minister knelt north with tucked tablet—powdered cakes before grain cakes, mash before fermented sauce, millet left and glutinous right before the grand stew, ox tray before dous, sheep, pig, and fish after, right uppermost.

sentences.zh: 司徒俯伏，興，奉饌者奉訖，皆出笏就位，一拜。

translations.literal: The Minister prostrated and rose; when bearers had presented all withdrew tablets, took station, and bowed once.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated and rose; bearers finished, tucked tablets, took station, and bowed once.

sentences.zh: 司徒次詣皇地祇奉奠，並如上儀。

translations.literal: The Minister next went to Imperial Earth and presented—all as above.
translations.idiomatic: He next presented at Imperial Earth by the same rite.

sentences.zh: 配位亦同。

translations.literal: The associated position likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The associated seat the same.

sentences.zh: 司徒及奉於、地、配位饌者以次降。

translations.literal: The Minister and those who had presented at Heaven, Earth, and associated positions descended in order.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister and Heaven, Earth, and associated bearers descended in turn.

sentences.zh: 太官令帥奉第一等神位之饌，各於其位，並如前儀。

translations.literal: The kitchen director led presentation of first-rank offerings at each seat—all as before.
translations.idiomatic: The kitchen director led first-rank offerings to each seat by the same rite.

sentences.zh: 俱畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When all were finished, music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: All finished; music stopped.

sentences.zh: 司徒、太官令以下皆就位，訖，侍中升自卯陛，立於昊天上帝酌尊所，以俟。

translations.literal: Minister of Education, kitchen director, and below all took station; when finished the attendant-in-waiting ascended by the mao stair and stood at August Heaven's wine station to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Minister, kitchen director, and others took station; the attendant-in-waiting climbed the mao stair to August Heaven's wine station and waited.

sentences.zh: 太常卿乃當次前俯伏，跪奏：「請皇帝詣盥洗位。

translations.literal: The sacrifice director then bowed prostrate before the tent, knelt, and reported: "Please let Your Majesty go to the washing station."
translations.idiomatic: The sacrifice director prostrated at the tent: "Please go to the washing station."

sentences.zh: 」俯伏，興。

translations.literal: He bowed prostrate and rose.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated and rose.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出次，殿中監進大圭，乃奏：「請執大圭。

translations.literal: The emperor left the tent; the palace director presented the great tablet; he reported: "Please take the great tablet."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left the tent; the palace director gave the great tablet; "Take the great tablet."

sentences.zh: 」至盥洗位，奏：「請搢大圭、盥手。

translations.literal: At the washing station he reported: "Please insert the great tablet and wash the hands."
translations.idiomatic: At washing: "Insert the great tablet and wash the hands."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝盥手，訖，奏：「請帨手。

translations.literal: The emperor washed his hands; when finished he reported: "Please dry the hands."
translations.idiomatic: Hands washed; "Dry the hands."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝帨手，訖，奏：「請執大圭。

translations.literal: The emperor dried his hands; when finished he reported: "Please take the great tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Hands dried; "Take the great tablet."

sentences.zh: 」乃詣爵洗位。

translations.literal: He then went to the cup-washing station.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the cup-washing station.

sentences.zh: 至位，奏：「請搢大圭、受爵」，又奏：「請洗爵。

translations.literal: At the station he reported: "Please insert the great tablet and receive the cup," and again: "Please wash the cup."
translations.idiomatic: There: "Insert the great tablet and receive the cup," then "Wash the cup."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝洗爵，訖，奏：「請拭爵。

translations.literal: The emperor washed the cup; when finished he reported: "Please dry the cup."
translations.idiomatic: Cup washed; "Dry the cup."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝拭爵，訖，奏：「請執大圭。

translations.literal: The emperor dried the cup; when finished he reported: "Please take the great tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Cup dried; "Take the great tablet."

sentences.zh: 」以爵奉爵官。

translations.literal: He gave the cup to the cup-bearing officer.
translations.idiomatic: He handed the cup to the cup officer.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣昊天上帝酌尊所，執爵，良醖令舉冪，侍中跪酌太尊之泛齊，酌訖，皇帝以爵授侍中。

translations.literal: The emperor went to August Heaven's wine station, took the cup; the director of fine brew raised the cover; the attendant-in-waiting knelt and poured wan-ferment from the great bronze; when poured the emperor gave the cup to the attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At August Heaven's wine station the emperor took the cup; fine-brew director lifted the cover; the attendant knelt and poured wan-ferment from the great bronze; the emperor gave him the cup.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乃詣昊天上帝神座前，侍中進爵，乃奏「請搢大圭，跪執爵三祭酒。

translations.literal: The emperor then went before August Heaven's tablet; the attendant advanced the cup; he reported: "Please insert the great tablet, kneel, take the cup, and thrice offer wine."
translations.idiomatic: Before August Heaven's tablet the attendant brought the cup; "Insert the great tablet, kneel, take the cup, and thrice offer wine."

sentences.zh: 」訖，奏：「請奠爵。

translations.literal: When finished he reported: "Please set down the cup."
translations.idiomatic: Done: "Set down the cup."

sentences.zh: 」奠爵訖，奏：「請執大圭。

translations.literal: When the cup was set he reported: "Please take the great tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Cup set: "Take the great tablet."

sentences.zh: 」俯伏，興。

translations.literal: He bowed prostrate and rose.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated and rose.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「請少退。

translations.literal: Again he reported: "Please withdraw a little."
translations.idiomatic: Then: "Withdraw a little."

sentences.zh: 」立俟。

translations.literal: He stood and waited.
translations.idiomatic: He stood and waited.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎讀冊文，訖，乃奏：「請再拜。

translations.literal: The vice director of the Secretariat read the prayer text; when finished he reported: "Please bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat vice director read the prayer; then: "Bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」詣皇地祇位及配位，並如上儀。

translations.literal: He went to Imperial Earth and associated positions—all as above.
translations.idiomatic: At Imperial Earth and associated seats—all as above.

sentences.zh: 獻畢，皇帝還版位，乃奏「請還小釋大圭。

translations.literal: When the offering was finished the emperor returned to the spirit-board station; he reported: "Please return to the small tent and release the great tablet."
translations.idiomatic: Offering done, he returned; "Return to the small tent and release the great tablet."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝入小次，太常卿立于小次東南。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the small tent; the sacrifice director stood southeast of the small tent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the small tent; the sacrifice director stood to its southeast.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引博士，博士引亞獻，詣次，盥洗位，搢笏、盥手、帨手、訖，詣爵洗位，搢笏、洗爵，拭爵，訖，以爵授執事者，執笏升自卯陛，詣昊天上帝酌尊所，西向立。

translations.literal: An orderly led the academic; the academic led the secondary offerer to the tent and washing station—tuck tablet, wash, dry; at the cup station tuck tablet, wash and dry the cup, give the cup to an attendant, take tablet, ascend by the mao stair to August Heaven's wine station, standing west.
translations.idiomatic: An orderly led the academic, who led the secondary offerer to wash and clean the cup, handed the cup to an attendant, and climbed the mao stair west to August Heaven's wine station.

sentences.zh: 執事者以爵授之，乃搢笏執爵。

translations.literal: An attendant gave him the cup; he tucked his tablet and took the cup.
translations.idiomatic: An attendant gave the cup; he tucked his tablet and took it.

sentences.zh: 執尊者舉冪，良醖令跪酌著尊之醴齊，酌訖，複以爵授執事者，執笏詣昊天上帝神座前。

translations.literal: The vessel officer raised the cover; the fine-brew director knelt and poured li-ferment from the zhuo bronze; when poured he again gave the cup to the attendant, took his tablet, and went before August Heaven's tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The vessel officer lifted the cover; fine-brew director knelt and poured li-ferment from the zhuo bronze; he returned the cup to the attendant and went before August Heaven's tablet.

sentences.zh: 初，亞獻至盥洗位，文舞退，武舞進，樂作。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the secondary offerer reached the washing station, civil dancers withdrew and martial dancers advanced; music played.
translations.idiomatic: When the secondary offerer reached washing, civil dancers withdrew, martial dancers advanced, and music played.

sentences.zh: 亞獻詣昊天上帝神座前，搢笏跪，執事者以爵授之，乃執爵三祭酒，奠爵，執笏，俯伏，興，少退，再拜。

translations.literal: Before August Heaven's tablet he tucked his tablet and knelt; the attendant gave him the cup; he took the cup and thrice offered wine, set down the cup, took his tablet, bowed prostrate, rose, withdrew a little, and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: At August Heaven he knelt, thrice offered wine, set the cup, prostrated, rose, stepped back, and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 次詣皇地祗及配位，並如上儀。

translations.literal: Next he went to Imperial Earth and associated positions—all as above.
translations.idiomatic: Then Imperial Earth and associated seats by the same rite.

sentences.zh: 獻畢，降復位。

translations.literal: When the offering was finished he descended and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Done, he descended and returned.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引博士，博士引終獻，詣盥洗位，盥手，洗爵，升壇奠獻，並如上儀。

translations.literal: An orderly led the academic; the academic led the final offerer to the washing station—wash hands, wash cup, ascend the altar and offer—all as above.
translations.idiomatic: An orderly led the academic, who led the final offerer to wash, clean the cup, ascend, and offer by the same rite.

sentences.zh: 初，終獻將升壇，禮直官分引第一等分獻官詣盥洗位，搢笏，盥手，帨手。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the final offerer was about to ascend, orderlies in turn led first-rank distributed-offering officers to the washing station—tuck tablet, wash, dry.
translations.idiomatic: As the final offerer was about to ascend, orderlies led first-rank distributed offerers to wash and dry.

sentences.zh: 執笏，各由其陛，唯不由午陛，詣神位酌尊所，執事者以爵授之，乃酌泛齊，訖，以爵授執事者，共詣神座前，搢笏跪，執事者以爵授之，乃執爵三祭酒，奠爵，執笏，俯伏，興，少退，再拜，訖，各引還本位。

translations.literal: Take tablets; each by his stair, never the wu stair, to his wine station; an attendant gave the cup; he poured wan-ferment; when poured gave the cup back; together they went before the tablet, tucked tablet and knelt; attendant gave cup; thrice offered wine, set cup, took tablet, prostrated, rose, withdrew, bowed twice; each returned to station.
translations.idiomatic: Tablets in hand, each climbed his stair—not the wu—to pour wan-ferment, thrice offered at the tablet, prostrated, bowed twice, and returned.

sentences.zh: 初，第一等分獻官將升，贊引引第二等、第三等、內濆內外眾星位分獻各詣盥洗位，搢笏、盥手、帨手、酌酒、奠拜，並同上儀。

translations.literal: Earlier, when first-rank distributed offerers were about to ascend, presenters led second- and third-rank and inner- and outer-enclosure star distributed offerers each to wash—tuck tablet, wash, dry, pour, offer, and bow—all as above.
translations.idiomatic: As first-rank offerers ascended, presenters led second- and third-rank and star-seat offerers through wash, pour, offer, and bow by the same rite.

sentences.zh: 祝史、齋郎以次助奠，訖，各還本位。

translations.literal: Scribe invokers and fast-officers assisted the offerings in order; when finished each returned.
translations.idiomatic: Scribes and fast-officers assisted in turn, then each returned.

sentences.zh: 諸太祝各進徹籩、豆各一，少移故處，樂作。

translations.literal: Each grand invoker advanced one basket and one dou, shifting them slightly from their former places; music played.
translations.idiomatic: Each grand invoker advanced one basket and one dou, nudged them slightly; music played.

sentences.zh: 卒徹，樂止。

translations.literal: When withdrawal was complete, music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawal complete; music stopped.

sentences.zh: 初，終獻禮畢，降復位，太常卿乃當次前俯伏，跪奏：「請皇帝詣飲福位。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the final offering was finished and he had descended, the sacrifice director bowed prostrate before the tent, knelt, and reported: "Please let Your Majesty go to the blessing-drinking station."
translations.idiomatic: When the final offering was done, the sacrifice director prostrated: "Please go to the blessing-drinking station."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝出次。

translations.literal: The emperor left the tent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left the tent.

sentences.zh: 殿中監進大圭。

translations.literal: The palace director presented the great tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The palace director presented the great tablet.

sentences.zh: 乃奏：「請執爵，三祭酒。

translations.literal: He reported: "Please take the cup and thrice offer wine."
translations.idiomatic: "Take the cup and thrice offer wine."

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「請啐酒。

translations.literal: Again he reported: "Please taste the wine."
translations.idiomatic: Then: "Taste the wine."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝啐酒，訖，以爵授侍中，乃奏：「請受胙。

translations.literal: The emperor tasted the wine; when finished he gave the cup to the attendant-in-waiting; he reported: "Please receive the blessed meat."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tasted the wine and gave the cup to the attendant; "Receive the blessed meat."

sentences.zh: 」侍中再以爵酒進，乃奏：「請受爵飲福。

translations.literal: The attendant again advanced wine in the cup; he reported: "Please receive the cup and drink the blessing."
translations.idiomatic: The attendant brought wine again; "Receive the cup and drink the blessing."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝飲福，訖，奏：「請執大圭。

translations.literal: The emperor drank the blessing; when finished he reported: "Please take the great tablet."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drank the blessing; then: "Take the great tablet."

sentences.zh: 」俯伏，興。

translations.literal: He bowed prostrate and rose.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated and rose.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「請再拜。

translations.literal: Again he reported: "Please bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: Then: "Bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」訖，乃導還版位，西向立，俟送神樂止。

translations.literal: When finished he guided him back to the spirit-board station, standing west, waiting until the music for sending off the spirit ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He led him back to the spirit-board, standing west until the send-off music ended.

sentences.zh: 乃奏：「請詣望燎位。

translations.literal: He reported: "Please go to the fire-offering station."
translations.idiomatic: "Please go to the fire-offering station."

sentences.zh: 」至位，南向立，俟火半柴，乃跪奏：「具官臣某言禮畢。

translations.literal: At the station he stood facing south; when the fire had burned half the firewood he knelt and reported: "Your subject [name] reports that the rite is complete."
translations.idiomatic: Facing south he waited until half the firewood burned, then knelt: "Your subject [name] reports the rite complete."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝還大次，出中濆門外，奏：「請釋大圭。

translations.literal: The emperor returned to the great tent; outside the central-enclosure gate he reported: "Please release the great tablet."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to the great tent; outside the central gate: "Release the great tablet."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝入大次。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the great tent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the great tent.

sentences.zh: 初，終獻禮畢，司徙、侍中、太祝各升自卯陛，太祝持胙俎進，減天、地、配位前胙肉加於俎，皆取前腳第二節，又以黍稷飯共置一籩，奉詣司徒侍中後，北向立。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the final offering was finished, the Minister of Education, attendant-in-waiting, and grand invokers each ascended by the mao stair; a grand invoker bore the blessed-meat tray forward, cut blessed meat from before Heaven, Earth, and associated positions and added it to the tray—each took the second joint of the foreleg—and set millet and glutinous rice in one basket together, brought them behind the Minister and attendant, standing north.
translations.idiomatic: When the final offering ended, the Minister, attendant, and grand invokers climbed the mao stair; an invoker cut blessed meat from Heaven, Earth, and associated trays—the second foreleg joint each—and set millet and glutinous rice in one basket, standing north behind the Minister and attendant.

sentences.zh: 俟皇帝至飲福位，太常卿奏：「請皇帝搢大圭啐酒。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached the blessing station the sacrifice director reported: "Please let Your Majesty insert the great tablet and taste the wine."
translations.idiomatic: At the blessing station the sacrifice director said: "Insert the great tablet and taste the wine."

sentences.zh: 」訖，司徒乃進胙俎，皇帝受胙，訖，奉禮郎贊曰：「賜胙。

translations.literal: When finished the Minister advanced the blessed-meat tray; the emperor received the blessed meat; when finished a presentation officer called: "Bestowing blessed meat."
translations.idiomatic: Done, the Minister advanced the blessed meat; the emperor received it; a presenter called: "Bestowing blessed meat."

sentences.zh: 」贊者唱曰：「再拜。

translations.literal: A presenter called: "Bow twice."
translations.idiomatic: A presenter called: "Bow twice."

sentences.zh: 」在位者皆再拜，送神，樂一成止。

translations.literal: All in attendance bowed twice; sending off the spirit—one movement of music, then stop.
translations.idiomatic: All present bowed twice; send-off music—one movement, then stop.

sentences.zh: 皇帝既入大次，更通天冠、絳紗袍，升輿，至齋宮，乘金輅。

translations.literal: After the emperor had entered the great tent he changed to the tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, mounted the carriage, reached the fast-palace, and rode the golden chariot.
translations.idiomatic: In the great tent he changed to the tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, mounted the carriage, reached the fast-palace, and took the golden chariot.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引門下侍郎當輅前跪奏，稱：「具官臣某請車駕進發。

translations.literal: The communications officer led the vice director of the Secretariat to kneel before the carriage and report: "Your subject [name] requests that the imperial procession depart."
translations.idiomatic: The communications officer brought the Secretariat vice director to kneel before the carriage: "Your subject [name] asks that the procession depart."

sentences.zh: 」至侍臣上馬所，乃跪奏：「具官臣某請車駕少駐，敕侍臣上馬。

translations.literal: At the place where attendant ministers mounted horses he knelt and reported: "Your subject [name] requests that the procession pause briefly and command the attendant ministers to mount."
translations.idiomatic: At the ministers' mounting place he knelt: "Your subject [name] asks a brief halt—command the attendant ministers to mount."

sentences.zh: 」侍中稱：「制可。

translations.literal: The attendant-in-waiting said: "The command is granted."
translations.idiomatic: The attendant said: "Granted."

sentences.zh: 」乃退，傳制稱：「侍臣上馬。

translations.literal: He withdrew and transmitted the command: "Attendant ministers, mount."
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and announced: "Attendant ministers, mount."

sentences.zh: 」侍臣上馬畢，乃跪奏，稱：「具官臣某請敕車右升。

translations.literal: When the attendant ministers had finished mounting he knelt and reported: "Your subject [name] requests command for the right of the carriage to mount."
translations.idiomatic: When ministers had mounted he knelt: "Your subject [name] asks that the right of the carriage mount."

sentences.zh: 」千牛將軍升訖，跪奏稱：「具官臣某請車駕進發。

translations.literal: When the Thousand-Ox general had mounted he knelt and reported: "Your subject [name] requests that the imperial procession depart."
translations.idiomatic: When the Thousand-Ox general had mounted he knelt: "Your subject [name] asks that the procession depart."

sentences.zh: 」車駕動，前中後三部鼓吹凡十二隊齊作。

translations.literal: The procession moved; front, middle, and rear thirds of the twelve bands of wind and percussion all played together.
translations.idiomatic: The procession moved; all twelve wind-and-drum bands of the front, middle, and rear played together.

sentences.zh: 應行禮陪從祀官先詣應天門奉迎，再拜。

translations.literal: Officials who had attended the rite went first to Yingtian Gate to welcome it and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Attending officers went first to Yingtian Gate to welcome the emperor and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 大樂令先詣應天門外，準備奏樂如儀。

translations.literal: The Director of Music went first outside Yingtian Gate and prepared to perform music as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: The music director waited outside Yingtian Gate to perform as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 訖，擇日稱賀。

translations.literal: When finished a day was chosen for congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When done a day was chosen for congratulatory rites.

sentences.zh: 承安元年，將郊，禮官言：「禮神之玉當用真玉，燔玉當用次玉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Cheng'an, when a suburban sacrifice was imminent, ritual officers said: "Jade for addressing the spirits should be true jade; jade for burning should be secondary jade.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng'an 1, before a suburban sacrifice, ritual officers said: "Spirit-addressing jade must be true jade; burning jade may be secondary.

sentences.zh: 昔大定十一年，天、地之玉皆以次玉代之，臣等疑其未盡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dading, jade for Heaven and Earth was all replaced with secondary jade—we suspect that was incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 11 jade for Heaven and Earth was all replaced with secondary jade—we doubt that was sound.

sentences.zh: 禮貴有恆，不能繼者不敢以獻。

translations.literal: Rites prize constancy; what cannot be sustained we dare not offer.
translations.idiomatic: Rites prize constancy; we dare not offer what cannot be sustained.

sentences.zh: 若燔真玉，常祀用之恐有時或闕，反失禮制。

translations.literal: If true jade were burned, fearing it might sometimes be lacking in regular sacrifices would in turn break the ritual system.
translations.idiomatic: Burning true jade might leave regular sacrifices short and break the system.

sentences.zh: 若從近代之典及本朝儀禮，真玉禮神，次玉燔瘞，於禮為當。

translations.literal: If we follow recent codes and our dynasty's ritual observances—true jade to address the spirits, secondary jade to burn and bury—that accords with rite.
translations.idiomatic: Following recent codes and our observances—true jade for the spirits, secondary for burning and burial—fits the rite.

sentences.zh: 近代郊，自第二等升天皇大帝、北極於第一等，前八位舊各有禮玉燔玉，而此二位尚無之。

translations.literal: In recent suburban sacrifices Celestial Sovereign and North Pole were raised from second rank to first; the eight former first-rank seats each had ritual and burning jade, but these two still had none.
translations.idiomatic: Recent suburban rites raised Celestial Sovereign and North Pole to first rank; the eight former first-rank seats had ritual and burning jade, but these two did not.

sentences.zh: 按《周禮典瑞》雲：'以圭璧祀日月星辰。

translations.literal: According to the "Canon of Regalia" in the Rites of Zhou: "Use gui and bi to sacrifice to sun, moon, and stars."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Rites' Canon of Regalia says: "Use gui and bi for sun, moon, and stars."

sentences.zh: '近代禮九宮貴神、大火星位，猶用《周禮》之說。

translations.literal: In recent rites the Nine Palaces honored spirits and the Great Fire star still follow the Zhou saying.
translations.idiomatic: Recent rites for Nine Palaces spirits and the Great Fire still follow the Zhou rule.

sentences.zh: 其天皇大帝、北極二位，固宜用禮神之玉及燔玉也。

translations.literal: Celestial Sovereign and North Pole should likewise use spirit-addressing jade and burning jade.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Sovereign and North Pole should likewise have spirit jade and burning jade.

sentences.zh: 」上命俱用真玉。

translations.literal: 」The emperor ordered all to use true jade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered true jade throughout.

sentences.zh: 省臣又奏：「前時郊，天、地、配位各用一犢，五方帝、日、月、神州、天皇大帝、北極十位皆大祀，亦當用犢，當時止以羊代。

translations.literal: Provincial ministers again memorialized: "In the earlier suburban sacrifice Heaven, Earth, and associated positions each used one ox; the ten great sacrifices—Five Emperors, sun, moon, Nine-Regions Earth, Celestial Sovereign, and North Pole—should also use oxen, but at the time only sheep were substituted.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial ministers memorialized again: "The last suburban rite used one ox each for Heaven, Earth, and associated seats; the ten great sacrifices—Five Emperors, sun, moon, Nine-Regions Earth, Celestial Sovereign, North Pole—should have oxen too, but only sheep were used.

sentences.zh: 第二等以下從祀神位則分刲羊豕以獻。

translations.literal: Second rank and below in associated worship had sheep and pig cut and offered in portions.
translations.idiomatic: Lower associated seats received cut portions of sheep and pig.

sentences.zh: 竊意天、地之祀，籩豆尚多者以備陰陽之物，鼎俎尚少者以人之烹薦無可以稱其德，則貴質而已。

translations.literal: We suspect that for sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, when baskets and dous are many it is to supply yin and yang substances, but when cauldrons and trays are few it is because human cooking cannot match their virtue—so only quality counts.
translations.idiomatic: For Heaven and Earth, many baskets and dous supply yin-yang things; few cauldrons and trays mean human cooking cannot match their virtue—quality alone counts.

sentences.zh: 故天地日月星辰之位皆用一俎，前時第一等神位偏用二俎，似為不倫。

translations.literal: Therefore sun, moon, and star seats all use one tray; earlier first-rank seats wrongly used two trays—that seemed irregular.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, moon, and stars use one tray each; earlier first-rank seats used two—that seemed irregular.

sentences.zh: 今第一等神位亦當各用犢一，餘位以羊豕分獻，及朝享太廟則用犢十二。

translations.literal: Now each first-rank seat should also have one ox; remaining seats receive cut sheep and pig, and for audience at the Grand Temple twelve oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Each first-rank seat should have one ox; other seats sheep and pig in portions; twelve oxen for Grand Temple audience.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: 」The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.
